arc.title: Session 1: Awakenings.
arc.text:
*Night. March 19th, 2012*

Tony’s mind wakes up. The sensations begin in his toes and fingertips. Eventually the limbs start to loosen, his eyes open. An awareness of liquid flowing down his parched throat. A man with a goblet is feeding you, sip by sip.

Lady Catherine had been honored by the choice to make her herald. She’s sensitive about her northern English accent, but money has opened doors for her. Her body feels electrified, as the decades of disuse meet against the flowing of blood once again. She remembers an old lover, a fellow kindred, and realizes that what she is drinking is potent, the vitae of another. It is stopped far too quickly, and she opens her eyes.

Dr. Banerjee is prone, coming out of the thickest brain fog.

Alice wakes up in a fog, but mostly oriented, and *famished*. She is still in the headspace of the ritual that put her to rest. She hears the muttered prayer to Mithras, notices the cultic markings on teh chalice. She is unable to speak yet, but observes the chalice get set down.

The four heralds slowly rise from their coffins and stand.

Alice: “Where are we? Who are you? Was the ritual successful?”

“I’ll answer everything, shortly.”

Introduces himself as Adalino da Silva. Explains that his job is to get them fed, clothed, and prepared to be briefed. This is a safe house. It is important to know that it is widely believed that Mithras is dead. We think it may be otherwise.

He brings them into an adjacent room where there are several people being held in cells. Some awake, some gagged, some unconscious. da Silva opens the cells and says, “Help yourself.”

Alice feeds from a young grocery clerk, but pulls herself back from fully draining them at the last moment.. Tony feeds from the older one. Tony is aware of how scared he is, but the man moves from fear to resignation.

Dr. Banerjee isn’t enthused that his victim is conscious, but is taking what he can.

arc.title: Session 2: Debriefing
arc.text:
*Night. March 19th, 2012*

*Dr. Henry Banerjee - player quit.*

Tony dresses slacks, loafers, collared shirt.

Alice wears something not too ostentatious.

Lady Catherine goes up to one of the young professional women, and turns on the *Awe*. “Oh my goodness, I would *love* to borrow that outfit for a day or two. Don’t you just look amazing.” The woman is star-struck, and agrees, strips off the outfit and hands it over. Catherine hands her a replacement from the pile of clothes.

Once they are clothed, they are brought up to the office of Darius Shirazi. It seems they are inside of a warehouse, various pallets.

The office, however, is classy; nicely polished wood and leather, books, etc. Darius is seated at the desk, and there’s a burly man (Mickey) seated in the room as well, looks like a fixer or bodyguard.

Darius introduces everyone, asks how he can be of assistance. Adalino excuses himself, taking the chalice with him.

Alice clocks that Darius is enthusiastic but very politic.

- They know that Roger de Camden was very close to Mithras, assisted with the ritual.
- They know that Queen Anne was also very close to Mithras, and had held London in his absence at times.
- Darius is forthcoming in answering their questions:
- ↳ Queen Anne has been Prince of London since Mithras’ absence.
- ↳ It is believed he died during the German bombing of London.
- ↳ However, the cult knows better; there was a traitor and an attempted assassination, but it is believed that Mithras still lives, in secret.

Tony soft-pedals a question that Alice gets blunt around: “Why weren’t we awakened as soon as Mithras was thought missing?”

Darius: “Because those same bombs brought the buildings above you down, and you were buried for decades. You were only just found, and that, accidentally.”

Darius hands a sealed scroll to Tony. He looks curiously at the seal, and then Alice takes it from his hands.

Lady Catherine looks at the seal, and remembers being intensely jealous of them. She looks over Alice’s shoulder and reads. Darius is clearly curious, but holds his tongue. Tony glances at it but does not read it in full.

Lady Catherine reads the message aloud, but omits the portion about the tasks to be done.

[Image: Untitled.png](campaign/assets/gm/fall-of-london-the-story-so-far-untitled.webp)

Alice comments that decorum demands they meet up with the Queen, make introductions again. Elysium is on Friday night, the Queen is hosting a party.

- They note that the letter says Lady Anne, whereas Darius calls her Queen.

Alice and Lady Montague recognize movement outside, and a couple beads of red light, hovering outside.

Lady Catherine flags it, and Darius spins around. Mickey jumps up and moves toward the door. Darius immediately opens a briefcase and starts moving papers into it.

Lady Catherine whispers that they can’t leave without the chalice.

Alice heads into the hall, and follows Mickey.

Tony waits outside the room, while Catherine tries to help Darius pack and encourage him that they need to leave *now*.

Adalino returns, and Tony says they need the chalice. Adalino hands it over.

Lady Catherine compels Darius. “We need to leave, *now!”* He looks around the room with despairing look, snaps the briefcase shut, and heads out. “We’ll leave through the basement, there’s a hidden exit.”

Tony follows, Adalino goes to support Mickey.

Alice sees Mickey hulk-out a little bit, and watches him leap off the mezzanine, charging forward. There are two officers in SWAT gear, and he leaps one and the other unloads a clip into him.

Alice runs back for the others, and seeing them missing, retraces her steps, eventually catching them as they head into a new stairwell.

Alice: “Darius, what the fuck’s going on?”

Darius: “Mickey and Adalino will buy us time, against whoever that threat was.” Leads them through a large drainage pipe and out onto a ledge by the Thames.

He leads them along the ledge, but Lady Catherine falls into the Thames.

They see a boat pull up to the warehouse they had just exited, and more figures exiting the boat. Catherine drags herself to shore, sans-jacket, and Darius brings them over to a white van. He unlocks it, goes to find Catherine, and then brings them all to a safe house.

They agree to not share unnecessary details with any non-Heralds.

Looking over the scroll again, they determine to check in with Alice’s old chantry and see if they can find Sri Sansa, to start.

arc.title: Session 3: Wednesday night
arc.text:
*Night. March 21st, 2012*

Lady Catherine: You find a posh apartment just as a wealthy, sharply dressed man arrives, speaking on a cell phone. You catch his eye, and use the free discipline Compel to say "Invite me upstairs." He nods and you follow him past the security guard and up to his penthouse apartment.

Once upstairs and in private, he abruptly ends his call and turns to you, grasping your wrist. You pull him into what begins as a kiss but ends in a bite.

You promise Oliver Kensington that you will return, and that he will welcome it, taking his credit card with him.

Waking up the next night, (Tues), Darius is already gone. They lay low Tues night.

Wednesday, Darius is still out.

Alice remembers that the chantry was in the basement of an old parish in Marleybone.

As they walk, Lady Catherine marvels at the styles and traffic density; Tony notices how noisy (but not loud) it is, and the hand held lit devices.

Alice notices people speaking into the air.

Lady Catherine is shocked and delighted by the fashions shown in the shops. Starts to make sense of class markers, etc.

When Alice arrives at the chantry, the markers have been removed. The building seems maintained, but largely unused. She looks for magical wards, but not only are they not there, they seem to have been removed. Alice goes around the back and finds a way inside.

~10:30 pm

It has very carefully been scrubbed of any evidence of ever having been a chantry.

They decide to go for a walk, explore the area around.

They get to the intersection, and there’s a petrol station. There are three toughs that are haranguing a woman who is leaving the water closet. Upon closer examination, the woman has some masculine facial features. Alice sees Tony tense, and is worried there’s about to be a masquerade breach. She touches Tony’s arm and uses Extinguish Vitae to try to force him to pause. Tony rebuffs her, goes into a blind rage, and uses fleetness.

Memorium: He has a vision of a time as a youth when he had been found out on the docks, and was getting beaten for masquerading as a man.

Tony comes to, and two of the three attackers are prone, seem dead, but Tony doesn’t particularly seem concerned. He is feeding from the third, and manages to pull back before killing the man.

The victim is starting to stand up, looks justifiably freaked out. Lady Catherine walks up and entrances her. “It’s going to be ok. Just look at me. Everything will fade away.”

As the victim leaves, her image burns into Tony’s mind. [New Touchstone] Alice feeds off of one of the other attackers, and then they make their way across to the shops at the strip mall.

The strip mall has a little fortune telling occult shop, a vintage clothing store, and a jewelry store.

Tony and Alice go to get their fortunes read. Alice sees the clerk behind the counter, and she strikes her as precisely the kind of eager young witch that she once was. The way she dresses, and her aura; someone who is passionate and dogged in seeking answers outside of the natural order.

Alice asks about the building where the chantry had been. The clerk is immediately intrigued; she doesn’t know anything, but there have been weird rumors, and then it had supposedly been cleared up because someone had a meth lab in the basement. Others believe it is haunted.

Tony gets called back for a tarot reading. *The Hanged Man, reversed. Stagnation, life not going as planned; may require action to take control of your life.*

Tony: “Is there a possibility for this to not end in fire and rubble?” *Herald of Pentacles, reversed. Paying the price of neglect. Too little, too late.*

The 30yo male fortune teller is apologetic. Encourages that these can be warnings of stagnation, not fatalistic. Tony finds the hints of stagnancy darkly amusing.

Alice’s turn. “What does the past say about the present?”

Memoriam: Alice is in a room, in front of a being, a god, emanating light. Worshippers surround, bowing to him, to her as a proxy to the god. She turns to the god and reaches out. She’s wearing a white robe, and grasps the hand of Mithras, and she is his handmaiden, and can feel his power flowing through her in a deep, deep connection.

Snapping out of it, the fortune teller hasn’t even drawn a card, but is just stunned. He pulls himself out of the chair and kneels before Alice, prostrate. “Heliodramus. Handmaiden. By the grace of Mithras it is wonderful to witness you again.”

Alice gently touches his shoulder, asks him to sit. “Where are our brothers and sisters?” As he draws the cards, she looks intently at him, and realizes that he is technically a vampire, but weaker than any she has ever met. A duskborn. An abomination, and a sign of the end of things.

*Three of swords. Rejection. Six of Wands.* Public recognition, victory, successes recognized. Both seem auspicious.

He explains that he was inducted into the Mithraic mysteries, and was sired by a Tremere, but lost his tenuous connections to the Camarilla court when the Pyramid (the Tremere hierarchy) fell apart when the chantry in Vienna was destroyed. This is devastating news to Alice. The entire Tremere council was killed, and the clan has split into warring factions. He said that his point person, Ayse, went west and gave them a contact named Najma, who could be found at the Roti Mojo [retconned] in Southall.

Alice asks about the primogen and the chantry. He confirms that Edward Bainbridge is still the Tremere Primogen.

Alice scrapes a nail across his wrist and flicks a drop of vitae into her mouth, using A Taste for Blood. She is horrified when she realizes this lick is fourteen steps away from Cain. She storms out.

Memoriam: Catherine faces the display in the jewelry store. She feels a finger on her shoulder, someone’s face against her neck, a familiar scent. Arms wrap around her. She’s not able to move, but feels completely at ease. An amulet is placed around her neck, and a woman whispers her love for her. The store front window is now a mirror and Catherine sees her face, sees the sapphire around her neck. The light from another room glints off of the sapphire. She turns to get a look at the person behind her but it’s just the street, everything is back to normal.

Instinctively, she touches her neck. She’s wearing a necklace, but it’s the one she took off of the woman at the warehouse. She realizes that the necklace in her vision may be gone forever. She walks determinedly into the jewelry store, and emerges bedazzled, having paid for them with her finance guy’s credit card.

Tony heads over to the vintage clothing store and similarly walks out with an new outfit.

They then head west, to Southall.

arc.title: Session 4: Wednesday night, continued.
arc.text:
*Night. March 21st, 2012*

The Puttanescas have their ways of knowing things, and were able to secret Matthias’ coffin from the rubble before even Darius could get to it. Matthias was awoken by a compatriot of Mithras, and oriented to the modern world.

Within 24 hours, a missive from Pater Thomas makes its way to Matthias as well, and he excuses himself to head out in search of the other heralds and the relics of Mithras, starting with a lead in Southall.

Lady Catherine excuses herself and promises to catch up later.

Alice and Tony lead west to Southall in search of Sri Sansa. Tony flags a cab, and the cabbie is an affable Egyptian who is delighted by Tony’s conversation, and “forgets” to charge them as they get dropped off in the heart of Southall.

Lots of teenagers out, not yet midnight. Cars blaring bhangra. Very lively.

Alice and Tony also notices the boys and that an older boy seems to be goading the fight. Tony is skittish after what went down by the gas station earlier, and they head in to the Roti Mojo.

There’s a line for tables and Tony tries to turn on the charm, flirting with the hostess to get a table. The hostess conspicuously flashes the ring on her finger, but when Tony mentions meeting Najma, she nods and brings them back through a curtain to a seating area with low couches.

An East African woman is finishing business with an older man, who bows and departs. The hostess tells Najma her guests have arrived. Tony and Alice seat themselves.

Alice uses *Sense the Unseen*. [Messy Crit] The beast in Alice rises in her throat, and she realizes Najma is another duskborn, an abomination like the fortune teller. She’s horrified about how badly things have gone to shit. She suppresses her discuss, but doesn’t extend a hand.

Alice: “We were told you might know where to find someone.”

Najma gets a read on Alice, that she’s Tremere. “Are you looking for Bainbridge, the primogen?”

Alice remembers Edward Bainbridge, who was Primogen even back in the day, but says, “No, Sri Sansa.”

Najma: “Why do you seek him?”

Alice: “Not your concern. Are you his gatekeeper?”

Najma: “I am not, but I know where his side entrances are.”

Alice: “Tell us, and I can ensure that you are adequately compensated.”

Najma: “A boon?”

Alice hesitates. “A trivial boon, perhaps.” This is not a negotiation between equals, from her perspective.

Tony: “I will reward you appropriately.”

Najma is unfazed by Alice’s flex.

Najma: “How about a vial of vitae? From either of you?”

Alice laughs scornfully.

Najma: “Then I think we are done here.”

Tony: “I can give you a vial of vitae.”

Alice: “What the fuck, Tony?”

Tony: “How else are you planning on finding Sansa?”

Alice is terse, but manages to hold herself back from physical violence. Najma pulls out some medic equipment, draws a vial of vitae from Tony. Najma thanks Tony.

Alice snatches the vial from Najma and holds it away. Najma bares her teeth at her; her teeth are laughably small.

Alice gives the vial to Tony. “Keep this. Do *not* give it to her.”

To Najma she says: “You will pass Sri Sansa a message to find me. There is no reward unless contact is made. If this happens, we will *consider* your request.”

Najma: “I know where to find him, tomorrow. I can give you that information now, but not without the vial.”

Alice: “Not happening.”

Najma takes a sip from a flask in her handbag. A mist envelopes Tony, who is blinded and starts to choke. The vial is removed from his hand. As Najma makes an escape, Alice spits venomous blood at her using *Scorpion’s Touch*. When the mist dissipates, Najma is gone. There is a piece of paper on the seat where she had been sitting.

[Image: Untitled 1.png](campaign/assets/gm/fall-of-london-the-story-so-far-untitled-1.webp)

Matthias took the trains and got completely lost in Southall in the process. Has grabbed one of the local free papers. Sees a group of young men/boys shouting, like a brawl is about to break out. Matthias studiously avoids them, buys a map from a corner shop.

Looking through the map, Matthias remembers a location where he had attended an Elysium in the 1930s. He makes his way over, ends up in front of the Blue Monsoon Lounge, looks like it hasn’t been updated in a few decades, but it’s modestly busy.

*Sense the Unseen* shows that it has been used by kindred, but not heavily. It seems too run down to have been the site of Elysium any time recently.

There’s a guy at the bar that is pretty sloshed that Matthias lures into the bathroom. He blocks the doorway with a trashcan, and muzzles him to shush the cries of pain as he feeds. Someone calls through the door, and Matthias tries to claim that his friend is just really sick and he’s helping. Matthias drains the man completely, and turns him to ash using *Ashes to Ashes*.

Leaving the bathroom, he almost walks straight into a woman wearing a hijab, looks Mediterranean. She looks at Matthias, and asks: “Was it a good feed?”

Lady Catherine sticks around, and ends up going to get her own fortune read.

The Star: Hope, a turning point, fair prospects for the future. The fortune teller remembers the name Angelique Darkwood as being a past member of the Mithraic cult, but has never met her nor knows of her current whereabouts.

arc.title: Session 5a: Wednesday, continued continued - in Southall
arc.text:
*Night. March 21st, 2012*

Catherine returned to the safe house. Alice and Tony aren’t there, but Darius is, reading something that he stashes when she comes in. She is hangry and has become paranoid (compulsion). “Where are they?!”

Darius: “They didn’t indicate.”

Catherine: “What are you reading? Why did you hide it?”

Darius: “I was reviewing a report, for Queen Anne, for Friday.”

Catherine snatches the Blackberry from him and asks what it is. He spends time walking her through how mobiles work. She can fumble her way through the basics, but is overwhelmed by the additional functions. He says that she can pick up a burner phone from one of the small shops.

She leaves, and goes to the banker’s flat. No one is home. Snooping around, she finds a laptop. A filing cabinet opens to her; stock certificates, bank accounts in the Caimans, etc. She gets enough that she can use a subset of the documents. The sums are pretty mind-boggling to her, in the millions of pounds. Does not find any connections to Lady Blackwood, or the Mithraic cult. The apartment is pretty austere, otherwise. Writes down the account numbers, etc.

When he gets home, he’s pretty inebriated, has a young woman with him. Catherine is in his bed. They are kissing and fumbling with keys and clothes, the woman pushes Oliver onto the bed and then sees Catherine and shrieks.

Catherine acts like she just woke up. “Darling, you brought a guest.”

Oliver stares slackjawed, drunk. Catherine is stunning.

The woman: “I thought you lived alone!”

Catherine extends her hand. “I’m Cat.” The woman is doing well for herself, but isn’t *rich*.

Things settle out, and Catherine gets them both to join her in bed. She feeds from them both, and then turns to the woman. “I’d like to give you a gift.” She bites her tongue, and gives her a kiss, feeding her a little of her vitae, beginning the process of creating ghouls. She does the same for Oliver. “You are a such a powerful man. You would like for me to be by your side.”

She convinces him to represent her business interests, starting her off using some of his own capital, and for him to introduce her to other people of power in the world of finance.

Oliver begins to get excited, he starts talking about alternative energy investments in the North Sea, and Bitcoin, which is still super early, etc.

Catherine encourages him to obtain a location for her to stay, and gives him the requirements for her and some ‘friends’. He commits to having one by Friday.

Tony stormed off after Alice tried to fight Najma.

Alice finds a phone booth and tries the number on the card. It rings a couple times, and then is picked up. “Psychic Healing.”

Alice: “Hi, I received this number from Najma, may I speak with…”

“Ah, you wish to speak with the guru.”

Alice: “Yes, if he’s available tonight, my name is Alice Mockingdale.”

There’s a pause. “The guru has retired for the evening. He will be meeting at Southall Library tomorrow evening, and new disciples are always welcome. We have an onboarding process for seekers, and perhaps you can ask the guru your question.”

Alice: “Thank you. I know him from *many*, *many* years ago. If you give him my name, he will understand why I need to see him right *now*.”

His tone becomes curt. “If you believe you know the guru from a prior life, I assure you he is quite a different man.” He hangs up the phone.

Alice tries calling again, but it eventually goes to voicemail.

Alice heads to the library he described. It’s closed, but she can use *Illuminate the Trail of Prey* to trace steps from the library. It looks like a large group. She follows it away from the main hub of Southall, and gradually the houses are getting nicer, it’s close to Osterly, there’s some gated houses, communities, the group is shrinking, until it’s too diffuse but there’s a 2-3 house area where it seems like the trail ends.

One of the houses stands out to Alice like the sun; it has all manner of wards, include some that seem hostile to Mithraic cultists. She successfully deactivates the ward against Mithraic cultists, but the fact that it was even there pisses her off. She does recall, however, that with a few exceptions (herself and Sri Sansa among them), Mithras generally held Tremere in extremely *low* regard.

Alice climbs over the gate, but the dress gets caught and she tumbles onto the other side. An automatic motion light turns on, and Alice scurries to hide. No one comes out.

She goes up to the side sliding door on this large house. There’s a clicking from another motion-detecting light, but the light seems burned out. She tries to get in, and finally gets frustrated enough she gains hunger and punches through the windows, gets inside.

The first floor is clearly a space for hosting, large open-concept kitchen, multiple fridges with pre-prepared platters of food, no blood (strange), large open area with pillows for sitting.

A wide staircase goes up to a mezzanine, and a tight circular staircase goes up to the second floor.

Before dawn, Catherine sneaks out. She doesn’t know where to find Tony or Alice, but she does remember where the Tremere primogen, Edward Bainbridge, lives, and makes a visit.

She rings, and a ghoul opens the door. “Lady Catherine. Would you please?”

The ghoul says “I’ll check,” and closes the door in her face. Returns later and says “He will entertain your visit, even if unannounced.”

Lots of artifacts, especially masks and statues from Africa. A room that previously must have been used for rituals, instead full of books and diagrams.

Bainbridge: “Ah, you have returned from burial it would seem.”

Catherine: “I had to reacquaint myself.”

Bainbridge: “It must have been a shock to come back and find your god is dead.”

Catherine: “You can’t truly kill a god.”

Bainbridge: “Well, then he’s doing as good a job of absenteeism as the Creator. What brings you here?”

Catherine: “I’m trying to understand the modern world, and would like you to help me with something.”

Bainbridge: “I’ll listen, but I’m not sure what you have to offer in exchange.”

Catherine: “First, I am looking for a Lady Blackwood. Second, a particular artifact; you are a curator of artifacts, are you not?”

Bainbridge: “I have a very *specific* collection. So, if it were to fall within my interests, I almost certainly possess it or know where to find it; if it is outside of my interests then I am likely of no aid.”

Catherine: “Mithras had a ruby ring.”

Bainbridge: “Well, I am not much for jewelry, but I know of the ring you speak of. And you said Blackwood? For tonight, I will waive payment, as the only information for you is unhelpful. The ring I believe is in the possession of Sri Sansa. He is no longer welcome in the chantry. He is trying to further fracture the clan and I will not tolerate it.” He gives a ballpark idea of where to find Sansa. “Blackwood was among the buried, during the bombings in ‘41.”

There is a profound feeling of loss and grief as Catherine hears these words. She knows, deep down in her heart, that Blackwood does not walk the night, tonight. And a memory comes to her, unbidden: that part of why she agreed to be herald was in the hopes that by the time she awoke, Blackwood might have awoken as well.”

Catherine: “Where is her resting place?”

Bainbridge: “That was decades ago, love. I wouldn’t even know where to begin.”

Catherine: “It was decades since we were buried.”

Bainbridge: “And look at what a bloody hard time it was finding you. It was dumb luck got you out of the ground. If you come to met at the Elysium there might be someone who knows where the body was last seen.”

Alice goes up the staircase and it opens up into a private study. It’s disorganized, and looks like it’s been half packed for moving in or out. The amount of obviously bullshit occultic texts disappoints. There’s a light further down a hallway.

She looks through some of the documents, and there’s a lot of details about moving people and items. Purchase of property, houses for a few dozen people, in rural England. Looks like Sri Sansa is trying to get out of London.

She moves down the hallway, and through the crack in a door sees Sri Sansa packing things into book boxes.

Alice opens the door, and asks, “Are you going anywhere?”

arc.title: Session 5b: Matthias
arc.text:
Confronted outside of the bathroom with “Was it a good feed?”, Matthias looks closely at the young woman, pegs her as Tremere.

“No such thing as a bad feed.” He’s ready to make a break for it.

“Are you here for the guru?” She tries to compel him, fails but doesn’t realize it. “Speak truly. Why do you seek Sri Sansa, *now*?”

Matthias plays along. “I was recently reawakened, seeking out old allies. I know Sri Sansa from many years ago.”

They find a booth, and she introduces herself as Ayse, a Tremere for House Carna, which she stresses. Asks if Matthias has opinions about the realignment of the Pyramid. Matthias has no idea what she’s talking about. Ayse weaves between talking about feminism, Islam, the Camarilla, “ever since Vienna”, and wanting Sri Sansa to support Carna’s claims.

Matthias lets slip that he’s been gone 70 years. Ayse puts the pieces together, and is awestruck, clasps his hands, and expresses her honor if he would escort her to the Ealing Library meeting Thurs night.

He asks about a place to stay that’s not too far, she says she has some rooms at the Meher Baba Centre. As they walk she explains how Baba’s understanding of Islam has helped her with overcoming the power of her beast within, temporarily.

They go into the downstairs of the centre, and there are secure rooms; modest but functional. Matthias does not trust her, but sees that she desperately wants him close and happy for her own ends, whatever they are.

Once secure and alone in the room, he begins to booby-trap the entrance, but starts to spiral into morbidity (compulsion).

arc.title: Session 5c: Tony
arc.text:
Tony calls the # that Najma left behind. The person who answers lets Tony know that the guru isn’t available, but will be at the library. Asks for and Tony provides a physical description of Najma, uses code that she looks ‘anemic’ (thin-blood); the person on the other end of the line says, “Ah yes, I know the type.”

As Tony stands in the phone booth, he sees an older woman raise a device and sees the screen capturing video footage of a group of youths, with two in the middle starting to fight with knives. Those around them shuffle around and eventually block the phone booth.

Tony uses *Cloak of Shadows* to hide themselves. They shift back towards the street, one kid connects and slashes the other, who drops their knife. A comrade pulls the arm up and starts lapping at the blood in a clear masquerade breach, captured on this hand-held device.

With a push with *Fleetness* Tony pushes out of the phone booth, snatches the phone from the woman’s hand, and grabs the indiscreet kindred over the other arm and pulls them into an alley.

He fights back but Tony has him in a headlock.

Tony: “What on earth were you thinking?!?”

Kindred: “I don’t know bruv, I can’t help it! … I was with my mates last week and this dope fiend jumped out from under the bridge and bit me. Do I need drugs? Is it methamphetamines?

Tony holds his arm behind him in a submission grip, has him lead them to the bridge. Introduces himself as Ferhat. No one is there now. They grab a cab, Tony uses *Awe* to cow the driver, and they show up in the safe house. Darius is there.

Darius gives his condolences that Ferhat was attacked, asks if he could give him an examination. Opens the mouth, notes Ferhat’s fangs are so small that they could not break skin. Darius brings some bagged blood, and Ferhat is sated but confused. Darius and Tony begin to give Ferhat a crash course on being a vampire.

Ferhat makes the connection: “Is that why Najma weirded me out?”

arc.title: Session 6 - Thursday
arc.text:
At Alice’s question, Sri Sansa looks up and his face goes even paler, but then Alice feels herself slumping to the floor, eyes fading.

Matthias wakes up to Ayse’s knock, disables the traps and locks, still is suffering the *morbidity* compulsion.

They head straight to the library.

Tony leaves Ferhat behind with Darius. Ferhat isn’t keen on being left behind, but Darius has been good and reasonable, and he trusts Tony a bit, for now. Tony heads to the library.

The library meeting room is filling up, with chairs around the periphery and then people standing or seated on small rugs and pillows. The elderly are mostly seated, the younger adults cluster around and gossip. Predominantly but not exclusively Punjabi. A couple “Eat Pray Love” types.

Matthias immediately recognizes Tony as both Brujah and Herald. He makes some subtle movements and allows Tony to reciprocate the recognition.

The room hushes, and a man in a suit enters, followed by the guru.

Meeting is called to order. Man in the suit gives an agenda, then begins taking requests from those gathered. A woman approaches, asking about her dead child. Sri Sansa hushes her, concentrates, and a faint voice of an 8 or 9-year old can be heard. Matthias and Tony are fascinated; it is no ritual like the Hecata, and if it’s faked it’s faked well. When Sri Sansa gazes around the room, his eyes dart away from the two of them and abruptly exits after whispering to the man in the suit, who apologizes and offers to answer questions.

Tony approaches. “I have a question for the guru.” The man offers a card for him to write the question down. Tony accepts it, and writes down a description of the ring he is seeking.

Alice awakens. It’s pouring rain, and she catches a glimpse of Sri Sansa walking on a cobbled street in an old suit jacket. She follows. A little girl, extremely poor, seems to pick his pocket, and Alice follows the girl and stops her. “I saw that.”

Girl: “You saw nothing.” She holds her hands open. Alice can tell she’s palming a coin behind her fingers.

Alice takes out a coin from her pocket, palms it like the girl, and then places it in her palm.

Memorium: Alice recalls when *she* was a child, in rags, offering to tell the fortune of strangers for a handful of pennies.

She lets the girl go, and then follows her for a while. Realizes this very much is not the 20th century. Eventually, she sees Sri Sansa again, and the girl picks his pocket again; it’s like a looped event.

Alice reads the girl’s aura, and realizes that *everyone* shares an aura, which seems extraordinarily odd.

While Tony writes on the card, Matthias speaks to the woman who lost her child. She did not witness the death, but was told it was a traffic accident. However, an unfamiliar agency in a black police van picked up the child, and she hasn’t received the body.

Matthias starts to put things together, and suspects that *if* there even was an accident, it was likely to cover up what would have been an unauthorized childer. It seems sloppy as well as foolish.

Matthias does not share his suspicion, but the matter feels settled in his own mind, and his compulsion exhausts itself.

Tony comes over.

Matthias; “I believe we are seeking the same person - Sri Sansa?”

Tony: “Yes, myself and the other heralds.”

Matthias: “Others?”

Tony: “There are two others I’m staying with. And a couple friends.”

Matthias looks around and sees that Ayse has gone as well. He has a *Premonition*, and remembers how intent Ayse had been on getting Sri Sansa’s support for House Carna.

They learn that these meetings are weekly, and there are invitation-only meetings at Sansa’s home as well. They are able to obtain the address, but decide to head to the safe house, first.

Tony briefs Matthias on Ferhat, and thin-bloods more generally, on their way. Tony is being a little tense, but Matthias doesn’t particularly care; Tony or this Ferhat do not seem like threats.

Darius is shocked and excited that another herald has been found, and barely contains his questions. Explains about his book.

Lady Catherine returns, and says that she’s found a penthouse to move the heralds to.

> Oliver is still furnishing the apartment, but lets you in and takes you away from the windows. A seeming wall opens into a small staircase and then a secret suite - a bunker seemingly designed for the hypothetical scenario in which nukes are flying and yet London apartments remaining standing.
> One bedroom features sleek marble accents and an en-suite bathroom. The other is tiled with a mosaic tessellation.
> Beyond the bedrooms lies the living area, a 12-foot river table dominating the space and giving it the feel of a board room. The tall-backed chairs reinforce the impression. The kitchen's granite countertops gleam,, and a spacious island awaits utilization.
> Security takes center stage within your safe room. State-of-the-art surveillance systems and reinforced steel walls guarantee your peace of mind.

Alice tries to catch up with Sri Sansa. A carriage crash happens right in front. One of the horses spooks and rears, breaking out of the harness but injuring the other who falls and tips the carriage. The people inside are bleeding.

The scent of blood is nearly overwhelming, but Alice recognizes the unreality of the whole scene and steels herself, follows Sri Sansa into a building where there is a seance in process.

A woman is in a trance. Alice stays hidden in the periphery. No one gives an acknowledgement of her presence.

She recognizes Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, and Justicar Justine Parr. There’s an older man in the corner who looks exactly like John Dee (but couldn’t be).

Alice again looks at the auras, and everyone shares the same aura. She starts to realize that this is an experience that Sri Sansa had, that she’s somehow inside of his memory; she’s not sure if this is a magical trap or effect or what.

When Alice’s eyes refocus, it is several hours later and the seance is completed, the room is mostly empty. She sees the John Dee-looking kindred put a hand on Sri Sansa’s shoulder and guide him into another room. She follows and listens in, and hears Sri Sansa receive a pitch, “our prince believes that your deep familial connections would be an asset to us. Let me take you to meet Mithras…”

Alice wakes up, and her brain feels thick, body feels heavy. She’s on a couch, and hears a woman and man talking.

The woman has a hijab, and a distinct aura, and the man is Sri Sansa; Alice can tell she’s no longer in the memory. The woman is arguing that Sri Sansa should support House Carna against House Tremere now that the Vienna chantry has dissolved.

Alice is able to understand that the memory she inhabited was not an effect that Sri Sansa had done, at least directly or intentionally. She sits up and listens in.

Ayse: “Wonderful, you’re awake. Could you help him understand how important this is?”

Alice says nothing.

Ayse: “You *are* backing Carna, are you not?”

Sansa: “I don’t think she understands that you are a herald.”

Alice folds her arms.

Sansa: “Why did you feel the need to invade my study?”

Alice: “I was looking for you. You weren’t at the library.”

Sansa: “I was at the library tonight, just like every Thursday night. I’m not hard to find. You didn’t need to break into my house?”

Alice: “Where are you going?”

Sri Sansa looks stricken, then brightens. “You never liked Bainbridge, did you?”

Alice shrugs. She and Bainbridge had challenges; as primogen, he technically was her superior, but her station as Heliodramus far exceeded his when Mithras was present.

Sansa: “Well, then, you probably won’t mind that I and some family and followers have found a lovely village in rural England where we have room and can be safe and secure. I’m sure Mithras, were he ever to come back, would understand, and would not in the least be inconvenienced by my absence.”

Alice: “Why does your property not welcome those of Mithras?”

Alice is trying to get a read, stands tall. She was one of the most trusted by Mithras, and here is this *fucking coward*, running away, *warding his property* against Mithras. Maybe at one time Sri Sansa was a true believer, but right now, even though Mithras is ostensibly dead, it is clear to her that Sansa is *terrified* of Mithras, and that he’s running from him and everything that reminds Sansa of Mithras. Alice becomes *paranoid*. Sansa was a trusted member of the cult, and remembers the letter of Pater Thomas “those once loyal”.

arc.title: Session 7: Queen Anne’s Elysium
arc.text:
Alice returns to the safe house, Darius is cleaning up and directs her to the new haven. The haven address is an apartment, it’s lovely and Catherine’s finance bro lets her in, and then opens up the wall to the safe room suite.

The others are settled, and Alice crashes.

When Alice wakes up, she realizes that a *thin-blood* is also here.

She shows off the ring, wearing it around her neck.

Lady Catherine calls the # Darius gave her, for party information. Lady Scarlett Churchill picks up; they had been business partners back in the 30s. They make small talk, and Lady Scarlett lets drop that she had given up both Catherine and Angelique for dead during the Blitz.

Memorium: Lady Catherine remembers clawing desperately through the rubble, and eventually finding the broken body of her love.

Lady Scarlett gives the address and instructions, and to ‘bring a gift’, then apologizes and drops off.

Lady Catherine takes blood from both of her ghouls as a gift, in small crystal vials.

They get to the Shard. Alice approaches the guards at the entrance indicated, and flashes her fangs at the guard.

They go up to the 66th & 67th floors, where the party covers. Lady Scarlett is majordomo and embraces Catherine as she exits.

“It’s so good to see you, you’re looking well.”

Catherine gives the vials, “A gift for her majesty.”

“I’ll make sure she gets them. It’s probably been a while; enjoy the Elysium. There are vessels for your enjoyment, to every taste. Do you seek an audience?”

Catherine: “If she has time for me, I’d be honored.”

Scarlett: “Then we’ll get you a slot.”

Matthias looks around. He knows Salvatrice Giovanni is almost certainly here, but he seeks out his contact Calogero Puttanesca, who is just exiting a conversation.

Matthias: “Thank you for delivering my mail, how did you obtain that letter so quickly?”

Calogero: “The cult of Mithras, while it is weak and dispersed, nevertheless has its ears and Pater Thomas has ways of knowing that I try to steer clear of. Please don’t take offense, but Queen Anne declared him dead decades ago, when she took power. It’s a lot easier for us now, honestly. I was surprised that Pater Thomas was still active.”

Matthias: “How has our family fared?”

Calogero: “Our family has fared well, with the most difficult challenge being the calcified court. The primogens are weak and insipid, and I think Queen Anne likes it that way; they are easier to control. But I think our clan’s interests would be far better furthered with a strong figurehead.”

Matthias: “Do you have someone in mind?”

Calogero: “That’s always the question, isn’t it? Before your return, the options were Salvatrice or myself. But Hecata presence is growing and warrants some constructive leadership, and not merely fawning at the Ventrue’s feet.”

Matthias: “I’ve preferred to lead from the background. The figurehead is, well, just a figurehead.”

Calogero: “I’ve heard that the group you arrived with has an audience with Queen Anne later. You might put in a good word for me, and see if she might be amenable to changing things up a little, even temporarily.”

Matthias: “I’ll see what I can do.”

Calogero: “Is there anything I can do for you?”

Matthias asks about Richard de Worde. Calogero talks about the Nosferatu more generally, their utilization of modern technology. Calogero is old-school, likes his informants to be flesh & blood; prefers no paper record.

Someone who looks like they could be a male model offers his wrist to Alice as an invitation, and she accepts. As she feeds she listens in on a dispute between a Nosferatu, Caleb, and a Ventrue, Natasha, about competing hunting ground claims.

Alice hears out their arguments, and pulls Caleb aside to ask about Richard de Worde. He says he can give a location to find de Worde.

Alice can tell that both are overstepping. Perhaps Natasha feels that the other Ventrue at court would have her back, and she’s throwing clout around.

Alice rules in favor of Caleb, and Natasha begrudgingly accepts the verdict. Caleb tells her that de Worde can be found at a particular subway station.

Lady Catherine saunters up to Bainbridge. “Did you find anything?”

Bainbridge: “What I have is a *lack* of information, that is hopefully helpful to you.”

Catherine: “How is that helpful?”

Bainbridge: “I have witnesses to her death, but none to her *final* death.”

Catherine: “And the location?”

Bainbridge hands her a slip of paper: “It’s all condos now. Ironmark Holdings.”

Catherine kisses his cheek. “Thank you.”

Alice hears a rumor in pieces from various sources, that Gwenllian ferch Arwyn is absent, and that her childe was supposedly killed by human hunters. Chun Hei has sworn vengeance and is around somewhere.

Catherine, Alice, Matthias meet up and seek out Chun Hei. On their way over, they see someone holding their legs, rocking gently.

She’s *hungry* and distraught.

Lady Catherine goes and takes two vessels by the wrists, and walks them over to the kindred. She hardly speaks, but grabs the man’s wrist and drinks deeply, switching over to the woman just in time. Bringing two was a wise idea.

Adisa: “Thank you. I didn’t think I would be able to leave the party without tearing something apart.”

Catherine: “Why did you come here so hungry?”

Adisa: “I lost Jerimiah. My retainer, my ghoul. I’m almost certain the mortals got him. I was just so angry and distraught, but the court needs to know, and then I got here and I just *couldn’t*.”

“I’m sorry. I’m Adisa, of the Banu Haqim.”

Catherine: “I am Lady Catherine, and we do have an audience. We could relay this information for you. Do you have shelter? A safe place?”

Adisa: “I have a haven, but I will not be staying there tonight. Tell the prince the humans are hunting us.”

Catherine: “We had our own run-in a few nights ago. If you need, we have room at our haven.” She writes the address and gives it to Adisa.

Adisa thanks her and leaves the party.

They continue and see Chun Hei, speaking with a couple other people.

Alice uses *Premonition* and can see that Chun Hei is basically vetting people. “Can I help you?”

Alice: “Perhaps we can help you. You’re looking for someone that you treasure?”

Chun Hei: “I’m looking for the killers of my sire.”

Catherine: “I’m looking for a fight. And we heard you might know where to find Gwellian ferch Arwyn.”

Matthias: “I like fights as much as the next man, if the next man doesn’t like fights. But tells us about who is missing.”

Chun Hei: “Zawadi was my sire.” She goes on to talk for a while; Matthias picks up on the fact that she knows Ayse, and his legal background lets him pick up on the cues that seem to indicate that Chun Hei is a bastard of sorts; an unauthorized childe. Normally they would be killed but it seems that Arwyn has found a way to keep Chun Hei around.

Everyone understands that Chun Hei is convinced that Zawadi was assassinated by humans.

Lady Scarlett finds them, bringing Tony with. “The Prince of London will see you now.”

They enter a VIP room and experience a flashback.

sections.title: Memorium:
sections.text:
They step out of a carriage. It’s 17th century fashion, and they are following someone into a large, gorgeous, quiet house at night.

Matthias recognizes the person in front as Valerius - the current Seneschal (although not present at the party), and the sire of Anne.

Inside, Anne curtseys deeply in a sumptuous gown, and there are three figures in the shadows across the room.

Anne: “I am honored by your offer of an embrace into a life beyond life. But I am a mere mortal, and there is a dilemma I simply cannot resolve. I have three competing offers, and they too have arrived here tonight.

- Nafessa al-Niazi (Brujah)
- Captain Jonas Cardoza (Lasombra)
- Lady Elizabeth Moorhampton (Toreador?)

arc.title: Session 8: Anne’s Embrace, Elysium Part II
arc.text:
They see Anne, but she already has the confidence and poise.

Alice remembers that Valerius was Mithras’ second-in-command, but that he fell out of favor when Valerius allowed the Camarilla to set up in England.

Alice suggests a coin flip between combat and intellect tests, and Anne says that she could’ve done that if it were merely a matter of fate.

They retire to the library, and Anne starts pulling books off the shelves, and asking questions of mathematics, science, the occult, medicine. Nafeesa responds with ease. Cardoza is ok with history and religion, but struggles with the other subjects.

As they watch Lady Moorhampton, they realize she isn’t actually Toreador.

A question comes up from British common law, and Matthias whispers a note on the provenance to Valerius, who answers confidently.

The questions on medicine, the answers Matthias assists with won’t make sense for another century or so.

It’s come down to Nafeesa and Valerius, and Anne pitches a debate between the two. You can tell that Anne delights in having these far older, far more powerful beings jump when she says jump.

Alice realizes that Moorhampton is Malkavian.

Valerius ends the debate, leaving Nafeesa speechless. Anne excuses the others, and takes Valerius to be embraced.

Shifting back to the present, Matthias and Alice are a little stunned. Lady Catherine is no longer present.

Lady Scarlet introduces Matthias and Alice as heralds, and that they came with Lady Catherine, and brought a gift on behalf of everyone, and sought audience.

Anne: “Well, you have my attention, I suggest you not waste it.”

Matthias: “We’re hoping to reintroduce ourselves, understand how we can best serve.”

Anne looks at them for a full minute in silence, then snaps her fingers. “I know where I’ve seen you before. Everyone? Please excuse us.” The room clears, except for Lady Scarlet.

Anne: “So. Mithras brought you forth. Is he back? Does he have need of something?”

Alice: “He’ll be back when he needs to be, but we are making preparations for his arrival.”

Matthias: “He keeps to his own schedule.”

Anne: “I’m all too familiar with that. Well, this is fortuitous; I have a task for you. You may have heard the rumors of Mithras’ death. In fact, I had to declare him dead to secure my authority in London. How did I know?”

Alice: “How did you?”

Anne: “Because the one who claimed to have killed Mithras, is my sire, Valerius. And I have a laid a trap for him. This very night, he believes he will be leaving London.”

Alice: “And where is he going?”

Anne: “To the final death. But I cannot imagine a more appropriate end than to have the heralds of the newly returning Mithras strike the final blow. I would give you a great boon for this.”

Alice: “Why the sudden need? He has looked after you for many years.”

Anne laughs. “Death at my hand, even through a proxy, will be a mercy compared to what Mithras would do to him.”

Alice: “How do you know it was him?”

Anne: “He confessed it to me immediately.”

Matthias: “Aren’t you concerned that Mithras will replace you?”

Anne: “I’ve always stepped aside when he’s returned in the past.”

They can tell Anne isn’t lying.

Lady Scarlet presents a dossier with location, route, etc.

Matthias is concerned that it’s a setup.

Alice has a memory, a flashback. She sees through her eyes, in a pool of blood. Anne is above her, bleeding into the pool Alice is in, and Mithras is behind her, in the 1940s.

Anne: “What will you need? I’m happy to supply you.”

Alice: “The seal, for one.”

Anne: “The seal? Oh yes, I don’t have it here, but I’m happy to provide it to you upon your return.”

Alice: “We’ll need it first.”

Anne: “I *already* have a plan in place, that does not require the seal. I was meaning transportation, firearms, or anything else. Take this #; it is to be used only if all other avenues have been exhausted.”

They bring in a couple of vessels, and Matthias fully drains one (1 stain).

They take the elevator behind the throne, to the sub-basement. Lady Scarlet gives them a key card so they can return the same way.

Matthias takes a pump shotgun with dragon’s breath rounds.

Alice grabs four Kevlar vests.

They put everything in the car.

Alice and Matthias conspire; perhaps they can merely put Valerius in torpor, make Anne think he’s dead.

Alice is concerned about the difficulty about killing an elder; it’s a death trap.

Alice thinks they should grab Tony and Catherine, and then talk to Valerius *before* killing him.

arc.title: Session 9: Warning Valerius
arc.text:
***Lady Catherine at Elysium***

After Lady Scarlett introduces them, Lady Catherine gets escorted to a side room and gets grilled by the sheriff of North London, Leticia Shy.

“Why did you choose to feed in a domain you did not have claim to?”

Catherine: “Forgive me. Upon my awakening I was given blood. I was under the impression that I would not be able to speak to the Prince until the Elysium; what was I supposed to do between then and now.”

Sheriff: “You may always seek an audience, and was the safehouse not stocked? Did Darius not provide, or an option to hunt on his grounds?”

Catherine: “Darius had *bagged* blood. It did not suit my taste.”

Leticia laughs. “And?”

Catherine: “What is my punishment?”

“You will owe a boon to the Queen, and until otherwise negotiated, please restrict your feedings to this domain.” Shy hands over a marked map.

Catherine: “Does that mean my bank guy is off limits?”

“Is he in this square?”

Catherine: “I can bring him there.”

Shy: “I will pretend I did not hear that. Please do not make the mistake of repeating yourself, or making me repeat myself.”

Upon Catherine’s exit, only Lady Scarlett is present.

Scarlett: “You missed some of the discussion while you were occupied. Can I bring your attention to something?” She brings out a dossier and begins flipping through it. “Your Prince has requested that you and your fellow heralds do the honor. This should speak for itself; please ask me if you have any questions.”

The dossier is the details on where Valerius is staying, the route he is taking tonight, and options for helping him see the final death.

Catherine: “So we’re wanting to kill this person?”

Scarlett: “The one who claims to have killed Mithras.”

sections.title: Elysium
sections.text:
Catherine bumps into Matthias, he confirms the assassination request.

Matthias: “We said ‘yes, your highness’, but we don’t necessary intend on following through; we suspect she’s trying to cover her tracks. She let it slip that *she* knows that Mithras is not dead, which invalidates the pretext to kill Valerius. I don’t really trust her.”

Catherine whispers: “Why don’t we turn it around and kill her instead?”

Matthias: “I thought of that, there’s just the wrinkle that she’s the bloody queen. We at least need more information, which we could potentially get from Valerius.”

Catherine: “As prince, she can authorize that killing, can’t she?”

Matthias: “Technically, yes, although this is not a blood hunt - so this is an extrajudicial killing. And she could always claim we did this on our own and call for a blood hunt on us.”

They mix and mingle at the party, hear tales of Mithras coming and going. There’s a sense by many that he is dead, but maybe that’s just a game we’re playing. Maybe he went east for the Beckoning. But to the extent that Mithras may have been killed by Valerius, it’s clear that he’s the primary suspect.

Catherine catches Lady Scarlett and apologizes, asks to relay a question to Queen Anne. Scarlett agrees to see what she can do. Catherine asks if someone excavate underneath one of Queen Anne’s buildings for Angelique.

Scarlett: “I do not object to work that can be done privately and without risk to structural integrity. I can put you in touch with someone to supervise, but it would have to be done within the fortnight.”

Catherine: “Thank you.” She reaches to embrace, but Scarlett takes the hand and just gives it a light squeeze. “I look forward to hearing back on your success tonight.”

sections.title: Tony at Elysium
sections.text:
Tony shows up at the party late, and finds Lady Catherine and Matthias conferring.

Tony: “Did Queen Anne have any information about the object we were looking to collect?”

Matthias: “Oh yes. Had a lovely chat. She said she had the seal, and would be happy to give it to us. Wanted us to kill her sire. You know, the usual.”

Tony: “Are we hitmen for hire, then?”

Matthias: “I’m not.”

Catherine: “I don’t think this is the right place to be speaking about it, exactly.”

Tony: “So if we don’t do this, we don’t get the seal?”

Matthias: “It’s not going to magically disappear, it just might not be as easily obtained without Anne’s permission.”

Alice: “She has affirmed that it is not present *here*.”

Tony flags down someone to seek audience, and gets brusquely denied. [Bestial failure]

“That’s outrageous! You can’t deny a herald!” Tony starts to throw hands, gets grabbed by two security ghouls. [Dominance compulsion]

Tony throws one off and twists around to feed on the other, who goes slack, goes into a dazed stupor, in time for the other to hit Tony square in the face.

Catherine: “Tony, Tony, Tony, they’re not worth it. Not the place, not the time.”

Catherine realizes they can leave now or Tony will be thrown out. Catherine smacks Tony on the nose, “Bad Tony!”

Catherine forces Tony to begrudgingly hold back long enough for Matthias to lead them to the elevator to the basement car park. Tony rationalizes it as being “better than the ghouls” in his restraint.

They argue in the car as to whether to return to their haven, or seek out Caleb and Richard de Worde, or seek out Adisa, or go through with the assassination.

Catherine contemplates buying time by killing the competition.

Matthias isn’t certain if it’s a trap meant to kill Valerius, or the heralds, or both. What if her sire is in on it? We don’t necessary know if he’s recruitable.

Matthias: “I think we send in one of us to do the talking, and the rest wait in ambush.”

Catherine argues that she might be able to seduce him.

Matthias: “You don’t know if he’ll be buying what you’re selling?”

They ultimately decide to send in Catherine, with Matthias going in second if she gets eaten or something.

They pull up to the Docklands haven. There’s a similar car parked nearby. Catherine walks up to the door, and buzzes. There’s a camera. She hears “one moment”, and then a security guard opens the door. “Come in.” He looks around. “Are there more?”

Catherine: “They are keeping an eye out.”

She is led down the hall and to a side room. A female security guard joins them, and they enter a sitting room where Valerius is seated.

Long hair, looks to be in his 30s, impatiently swiveling, holding a book to his chest. “This is a little different.”

Catherine: “I have come to pick you up.”

Valerius: “Sounds like things are arranged with Jack and Diane here. Are you ready to go?”

Catherine: “Are Jack and Diane going first?”

Valerius: “Oh, they’re my bodyguards, they’ll be coming with me.”

Catherine: “Could I give you a message from her majesty, first? Privately?”

Valerius: “You may speak freely in front of them.”

Catherine gets frustrated. “Shit goddamn motherfucker!” She looks about, gets on her knees and reaches up to Valerius. “Your life is in danger. Anne sent us here to kill you.”

Valerius: “And you have evidence of this?”

Catherine reaches into her bag. Jack keeps his hand on his holster. She presents the dossier, and Valerius flips through it. He murmurs, “that conniving bitch,” with admiration.

Jack: “The others in the car… they know that you’re saying this?”

Catherine: “They know.”

Jack: “So they are not a threat to Valerius.”

Catherine: “They are not.”

Jack: “I recommend we stick to the existing plan, knowing that we’re on the same page of getting Valerius safely out of London, and out of Anne’s clutches.”

Catherine: “I would like to ask you something, as a herald of Mithras.”

Valerius: “I *knew* I recognized you!”

Catherine: “You have been accused of killing him.”

Valerius: “And yet you warn me, to save my life.”

Catherine: “I am not the type of person to pass judgment without proof. I want proof that you’re the one that killed him. Either way, I’ll save you today.”

Valerius: “I do not know what proof of me you would seek. There is nothing left of Mithras. I captured his lover. I had discovered the lover’s identity, and I knew that bait would bring Mithras. I lured him to the Gunpowder Mills, and once he entered we blew up the entire building. I watched and waited for months to make sure he was gone. And then I told Anne. Do you still wish to pardon me?”

Catherine: “Why did you it?”

Valerius: “You’re a Ventrue. You have a sense of what power can accomplish. Mithras accomplished a phenomenal amount for London, but had no vision for *England*. No vision for *Europe*, or the world. The Camarilla did. I brought them here, and I was punished for it. I brought a vision of a greater, united kindred across the United Kingdom, across Europe; where we could leverage our power. And Mithras only had eyes for London, and was deeply myopic in that respect. When his reprisals upon me, and demotion came to be, I bit my tongue and bade my time.”

Catherine leans forward and whispers “The only real reason I decided to become one of his heralds was so I could awake and be reunited with my sire.” She straightens. “I will pretend I have not heard your confession, and I will still save you. Come on.”

Valerius nods to Jack and Dianne. They grab some remaining bags and head out.

Unbeknownst to Catherine, Matthias has been piggybacking on her senses throughout this exchange. She is none the wiser, and he does not tell the others.

Jack offers to drive one vehicle. Matthias and Alice join.

Valerius and Diane take the other car. Tony and Catherine join.

As they start to drive, Jack turns to Alice and Matthias. “Are you also heralds of Mithras?”

Alice doesn’t respond. Matthias laughs. “Do I look like a bloody herald?”

Jack apologizes. “Sorry, my mistake.”

arc.title: Session 10: Jesus take the wheel
arc.text:
Matthias maintains *Share the Senses*, continuing to observe Catherine.

Catherine raises the partition so that Diane and Valerius can have privacy, and so can she and Tony.

Catherine: “Ok Tony, I plan on having him killed, but not tonight or anytime soon. He’s worth more alive than dead to us now, and has powers we could not otherwise access. We’ll take him to our safe house, and I’ll have my banker arrange a flight. While we’re waiting maybe we can get more information from him. But we cannot take him to the warehouse, in case the other assassins are there.”

Catherine then lowers the partition. “Seneschal, here’s what we’re going to do. There was no pick-up car. We’re going to take you to one of my places. I have a contact who can arrange for safe transit. I just need you to trust that we have your best interest at heart.”

Valerius looks concerned, confers privately with Diane, then says. “I appreciate your candor. The address?”

Tony: “How about your guy tails us?”

Valerius: “Jack is perfectly capable of following you, but if we end up being followed they can throw off the tail and then reconvene.”

Tony: “That’s… perfectly reasonable.”

Catherine provides the address.

Diane calls Jack over her radio, gives a code phrase and then “Change of destination. We’re going to lead, you’re going to follow.” and she provides the address.

Matthias sees Jack plug the address into some kind of device, then allows Tony to pull ahead.

Alice recognizes that the address is the new haven that Catherine has arranged.

Tony: “Is there anything we could present to Queen Anne that would convince her of your downfall?”

Valerius: “If you try to fake Anne out, it’ll only last so long; and then you’ll need an exit strategy as well. Your best defense is a good offense. That said, I know of some of her safe houses, and you could potentially find something of worth there. But if you’re launching a coup, you’re on your own.”

Catherine: “Valerius. Why are you trusting me?”

Valerius: “Trust isn’t binary. I don’t trust you, but I distrust you less than many in this court. And those that I trust have seen fit to trust you. And to be perfectly frank, even the fact the queen has entrusted you with this is a compliment all its own, even if you choose to be unworthy of that trust. Her assessments are rarely this far wrong.”

Tony realizes that he might recognize them as heralds; doesn’t say anything.

Catherine: “You are an elder, and have centuries of experience. Why do you suppose Queen Anne wanted you dead?”

Valerius smirks. “Why does any Ventrue do anything? What does my death benefit her?”

Catherine: “Power. But she’s already in the most powerful position.”

Valerius: “And when you are *in* power, you want to *maintain* power. And where are your greatest risks to power? Those that brought you to power.”

Tony: “Why aren’t you in that power, instead of her?”

Valerius: “I have the flaw of vision, of a vision greater than myself, where I could recognize that another was more suited to implementing it.”

Tony: “Do you feel that Anne still deserves the position she holds?”

Valerius: “Honestly, I would’ve done the same were I her in shoes. She’ll deny this, or worse, if you speak of this to anyone. But she has diabolarized, and in many ways is now more than my equal.”

Catherine: “That’s why she wants you dead; you know her secret.”

Diane’s radio crackles, and Jack says, “There’s an upcoming blockade, I know of an alternative route. Let me lead.”

Matthias does not see evidence of a blockade ahead, or on the digital interface Jack is referencing.

Jack’s car is accelerating and moving in front of Tony’s car. He turns to Alice and Matthias and says, pointedly, “Sometimes the bull must be slain.”

Matthias recognizes this as a Mithraic reference, but doesn’t understand how it’s relevant to the current situation. Alice somehow misses the reference.

Jack signals to take an exit. Matthias uses *Arms of Ahiram* to strangle Jack, and tries to take the wheel. Jack evades and wrenches the steering wheel, flipping the car.

Tony sees the car in front of him turn and flip, and barely dodges the car, scraping the right side. They pull off about 20 yards ahead, trying to figure out what’s going on.

Catherine: “What the fuck is going on? Diane, what the hell?” Catherine turns around and sees Diane wielding a stake, trying to get Valerius. Valerius rips through his seatbelt, and moves quickly up and to the side. His eyes go cold, and he rips her throat out.

Tony thinks, “Oh no, they’re on Queen Anne’s payroll and now she knows our safehouse location and betrayal.”

Jack’s car stops, upside down, but it’s not on fire. The shadow arms have grappled Jack. Alice extricates herself, and spits a paralytic poison on Jack using *Scorpion’s Touch*.

Matthias gets out as well and storms past Alice, considering using the shotgun but remembers the dragon fire rounds and resorts to his fists, wounding Jack and trying to kill him.

Alice tries and fails to get Matthias to stop, and finally insists, “As your Heliodramus I command you to cease! Let me question him, first.”

Matthias: “Two minutes, then we need to get out of here.”

In Tony’s car, Tony recalls they’ve been asked to chauffeur Valerius. Is given an address, and drives off. Catherine resists the domination [messy crit]. *You’re trying to dominate another Ventrue?* Catherine goes with the flow to see where they’re being taken.

Alice and Matthias see the car drive off. Matthias tells her, “I can find our friends wherever they are.”

Alice: “Ok, let me ask a couple questions and then let’s go to the old chantry.”

Alice makes sure Jack is conscious, then asks, “Anne sent you, didn’t she?”

Jack: “Why would I work with that usurper?”

Alice: “Why did you try to kill us?”

Jack: “Have you so forgotten your lord? I serve the same.”

The realization sinks in that Jack is a Mithraic acolyte.

Matthias releases the shadow tentacles.

Jack: “You seek his return as well?”

Alice: “You know who I am.”

Jack: “Then you know why Valerius must die.”

Alice: “Are the rumors true? Did Valerius kill him?”

Jack: “He did his best.”

Matthias: “Do you have orders from our Lord? Or were you running off on your own doing stupid things.”

Jack: “It is an edict from his own lips.”

Alice can tell that Jack truly believes what he’s saying.

Alice: “Matthias, we can’t kill him just yet. Let’s take him with us.”

Valerius, Catherine and Tony end up at a safe house.

Alice, Jack and Matthias take a cab to the former chantry.

Alice uses a *Taste of Blood* on Jack. [Bestial Failure, consequences TBD].

Matthias uses *Spirit’s Touch* on the digital tablet from the car. He forms a hazy sense of a person prior to Jack; perhaps a kindred of the Banu Haqim, or Ventrue? Middle-aged, facial features cannot be made out. Perhaps this Ventrue muddled Jack’s mind, made him think he’s Mithras.

arc.title: Session 11: Safe and Unsafe Houses
arc.text:
Alice, Matthias, and Jack arrive at the chantry in a cab. Alice leads them inside and they resume interrogating Jack.

Matthias saw through Catherine’s eyes that Valerius had killed Diane, ordered Tony to drive away before he lost contact. Tony and Catherine both appeared ok.

Matthias is making himself look relatively weak and unthreatening (Show Your Belly), and Jack is becoming more at ease. Jack becomes deeply distressed when he learns about Diane’s death.

Matthias: “What do you know about Queen Anne?”

Jack: “Queen Anne has been trying to put Valerius out to pasture for a while now. Valerius has been trying to make contingency plans. We’ve learned of a few stash/safe houses Anne kept that were secret from the court. If you want to deal with Valerius for good, I would start there.” He gives the addresses of two of them.

Alice: “You mentioned that Valerius did his best. What did you mean by that?”

Jack: “I mean, that he *believes* that he killed Mithras. But we *know* he was unsuccessful.”

Alice: “How exactly did you encounter Mithras? In a vision?”

Jack: “He sought us out, in physical form.”

Alice glares at Jack for a moment, orders him not to go anywhere, and pulls Matthias aside in an adjacent room.

Matthias explains that the image of the vampire he sensed looks *nothing* like Mithras, but that Jack seems convinced.

Given that Jack seems sincere, Matthias thinks that they should check out the safe houses.

Alice resolves to retry Jack’s blood. Matthias offers to get the blood for her. He returns, and Alice tastes the blood, and the memories flood back. Jack ***is*** blood-bound, to Mithras himself.

She is stunned, and relays this to Matthias. Matthias wracks his brain, and recalls that at least in diablerie, it is possible for vitae to overtake its host. Perhaps the image of the Banu Haqim or Ventrue that Matthias saw is Mithras, now in a new body?

Perhaps with research with the Hecata or Tremere, he could learn more.

Matthias is hungry, and starts to go to feed on Jack, but Alice stops him, insisting that now that they know Jack is blood-bound to Mithras, it would be better to find someone along the way.

They head out, and Matthias finds someone on the side of the street that he feeds on while Alice and Jack cover, then they get a cab to the first of the two addresses.

Lady Catherine’s mind races as Valerius directs Tony turn-by-turn, first seemingly to lose a tail, and then into the financial district. They pull into an apartment parking garage, and walk around to a door on a side street. Valerius enters a keypad code and leads them up to one of the second floor apartments. He enters the code.

The apartment is furnished elegantly but comfortably, but hasn’t been occupied in quite some time. Tony flops down on a chair. Valerius paces.

Catherine offers to go get Oliver’s assistance with getting Valerius out of London. Valerius acknowledges the offer but defers, instead removing a painting and entering a third code into a keypad that opens up a vault door.

It’s similar to her new haven, but definitely not a rush job, and looks almost like a museum. There’s a gorgeous Victorian dress on a mannequin, and jewelry and old books and diaries and pamphlets, all going back to the 1900s, 1800s, 1700s…. 1600s?

And there, in a glass enclosure, is Mithras’ seal.

Catherine: “Valerius. Could I have this little trinket here?”

Valerius is taking books and putting them into a banker’s box. “Take whatever catches your eye. I have no use for it.”

Catherine pockets the seal, and then goes and finds luggage in the bedroom and starts packing the dress, some of the papers, and then moves to the jewels.

As she goes through the jewelry, there’s a piece that stops her dead; a necklace from Angelique, that she had worn at the ritual in the 40s.

Catherine holds it up accusingly at Valerius. “Where did you get this?”

Valerius looks at her blankly. “This is Anne’s collection, not mine.”

Catherine fumes. “Really? That bitch stole it from around my neck while I was in slumber?”

Valerius resumes his work.

Catherine lovingly and gently puts the piece around her neck, and resuming casing the joint without remorse.

Alice, Jack and Matthias get dropped off at the first address. They tell the cabbie to wait, and walk up. Matthias stares at they exterior keypad for a moment, and then Spirit’s Touch reveals the code and he enters it confidently. The door opens, and he follows the spirit influence up the stairs and to the second floor apartment, where again the code is entered confidently and they enter a lovely furnished apartment.

They look around and then split up to check the rooms. Matthias enters the master bedroom and sees an anti-terrorism officer and an intelligence agent. The wardrobe is open, all its contents dumped onto the bed, and a vault revealed in the back of it. The intelligence officer has a number of wires connected to the vault and to his laptop on the floor where he is sitting.

The other officer sees movement and Matthias and he snaps his rifle up and fires just as Matthias brings forth two tendrils of shadow. The incendiary round scorches Matthias painfully despite the Kevlar, and the shadows begin to constrict and torment the men.

Jack and Alice run in. Alice spews venomous vitae but the anti-terrorism officer dodges it and is sizzles against the wall. Jack rushes forward and the man pulls his sidearm and shoots Jack through the collarbone, and Jack stumbles down.

The tendrils constrict further, and the two men lose consciousness. Matthias is wounded, but not mortally. He tends to Jack and stabilizes him, and then looks to the laptop. He sees that it appears to be running a codebreaker on the vault, and has another 30-45 minutes to go.

Matthias calls out, “It’s safe to come out now.” in case there was someone in the vault hiding, but there’s no reply.

Alice takes the weapons from the unconscious men, handcuffs and searches them. She finds multiple forms of identification or security clearance tags, including from GCHQ (on both), JTRIG (Joint Threat Research Intelligence Group), SO13, Antigen (on both), and ECTU (only on the one with the laptop).

Matthias notes that the weaponry matches what Queen Anne had offered them. “Are these perhaps her personnel?”

Alice asks Jack about the different acronyms, but he’s only able to offer limited information.

They wait for the codebreaking, and when the vault opens they enter it. It is similarly outfit to the vault where Catherine and Tony are,

They barricade themselves in the vault as dawn approaches.

arc.title: Session 12: Saturday: Going Underground
arc.text:
Alice and Matthias awaken on Saturday night, Jack having continued to watch over the two handcuffed and gagged men. After some discussion, Alice goes to find the station that Caleb had indicated she should go to to find Richard de Worde, and Matthias agrees to meet her there.

Alice takes a Mithraic cultic outfit, and three of Valerius’ journals.

Catherine calls Oliver, has him set up a private flight for Valerius, and instructs him to sabotage the flight so that it will blow up mid-flight. She organizes this unilaterally, believing that Valerius has served his purpose for her.

She wakes to a missed call from him. She calls back and he says, “Everything in in place. Come see me for details.” Catherine lets Tony know that she’s heading out.

Tony uses the time to ask questions about de Worde and Arwen of Valerius.

Valerius is shocked to hear Arwen’s name. “She is on the Red List.” [basically, a Most Wanted - kill on sight, there’s a reward for her destruction due to her rumored diablerie of Prince Jackdaw of Bath.] “Arwen had been spreading tales of Mithras joining the Sabbat, which also didn’t win her many friends.”

Sidenote: You can want someone killed but still want their reputation unsullied. Valerius had great fear and respect for Mithras even as he opposed him. He believed Mithras was *wrong*, not that Mithras was dishonorable or evil.

Regarding de Worde, Mithras shares: “Mithras’ weakness was his lover, Roger de Camden. However, no one knew what de Camden looked like. My plan fell into motion when I was approached, unsolicited, by de Worde who offered the information that de Camden was in fact disguised as Pater Thomas. I used that information to plan the lure for the attack that killed Mithras.”

de Worde has basically barricaded himself underground, using magical means to dissuade other kindred from pressing in, unwanted.

Tony recalls meeting Chun Hei, the childe of Zawadi (who Chun Hei believes was killed by hunters), the childe of Arwen.

Catherine meets up with Oliver, and he pulls up an itinerary; a chartered flight, leaving a NW London airport. He has it on good authority that it will explode over water on its way to Scotland. Catherine congratulates him, and gives him more of her vitae.

Oliver: “Anything you require; I will move mountains to accomplish.”

Claire comes over while Catherine is present and asks, “Did you see the news about the hostage situation?”

Catherine: “Enlighten me.”

Claire: “They said terrorists took over a section of the Shard, they evacuated the rest.”

Catherine is shocked. “Did they say anything about casualties named?”

Claire: “They haven’t released any information about casualties or hostages, but the news hasn’t shut up and there was an annoying security cordon downtown I had to navigate through to get here. It was a pain in the ass.”

Catherine kisses Claire and gives her a taste of vitae as well. Claire’s shoulders relax as her tension evaporates.

Catherine has Ollie drive her back to the safe house, making sure they aren’t followed.

Upon return, Catherine explains the itinerary. Valerius picks up two duffle bags, mostly filled with books and documents. “I have what I need, so I’ll have your chauffeur take me straight to the air field.”

Catherine: “Additionally, a mortal spoke of a terrorist attack on the Shard where Elysium was held last night.”

Valerius: “It’s not impossible, but Queen Anne’s enemies are far from limited to mortals, and this seems like a useful pretext. It is best I exit the city sooner, although it would be delicious if in a way her attempts on me resulted in her own demise.”

Catherine whispers to Tony after Valerius leaves, “We have what we were looking for; tonight that motherfucker’s going to fry.”

Tony is stunned but says nothing.

Catherine and Tony make it back to the apartment, and they see Adisa, the Banu Haqim from Elysium. Ferhat is speaking with her, and Claire is taking care of things, looking confused.

Adisa: “Oh thank goodness. You heard about the attacks?”

Catherine: “Yes, do you know anything about them?”

Adisa: “I left before you did, I hoped you would know. But I hope it’s ok I took you up on your offer; I didn’t feel safe in my haven after everything.”

Tony: “We were sent on an errand by Queen Anne, just finished.”

Catherine: “We should probably check in with her. Not sure how.”

Alice approaches the stairs down to the station silently, sneaking past the police officers and dog that are casually keeping an eye on the area.

The station is defunct. There’s another figure in the shadows; young man, button-up shirt and khakis. He’s aimlessly walking around. At one point he catches a rat and feeds off of it.

She continues pressing forward, finding the station that Caleb mentioned and sensing a way forward through the tunnels that feels magically oppressive.

Her neck tingles and she freezes, feels like she’s being watched. She holds herself utterly still. She stares right at the subway way, and sees a part of the shadow rotate around and climb up and then crawl deeper into the tunnels. A low growl is heard.

Alice retreats until she sees the young man again. She emboldens herself and goes back down into the tunnels.
