Claire, Adisa, Tony, and Catherine also arrive. Claire walks up to the police and serves to distract while the other three make their way down.

The young man walks up to them. “Oh hi there, are the police gone? My name’s Victor.”

Catherine: “No, the police are still here.”

Victor is crestfallen. “Oh. How did you get through then? Are you looking for the club as well?”

Catherine: “We’re supposed to be meeting someone.”

Victor: “Same here!” He pulls out a folded piece of paper and displays it. It seems to be a promotional flier for a ‘Lonely Persons’ Club’. “I’ve been here for three days but no one else has been through and I can’t find the door or get past the police.”

Catherine: “Well, a friend of mine was supposed to show up.” She describes Alice.

Victor: “Well I haven’t seen anybody, but if you’re down here long enough it feels like you’re being watched.”

They followed, and came up on Alice.

Catherine talks about the Shard being attacked, and connects it to what Alice shared about the humans she encountered.

arc.title: Session 13: Ambushed
arc.text:
Matthias arrives late, sees a woman (Claire) and two officers, and a police van driving away. He finds a broom and bucket and tries to pretend to be a janitor and go down the stairs. The female officer taps his shoulder, tells him “the station’s closed, it’s off limits.” Matthias fakes an Italian accent, tries to pretend to not understand and is acting stressed out, like he needs to get to his job on time. He pushes forward, she grabs his arm. The other officer, a burly man, moves forward but the dog on the leash is freaked out and doesn’t want to approach Matthias.

Matthias senses this isn’t going to work, and dropping the broom and bucket, darts down the stairs. He arrives at the bottom, and no one is there. He moves into the shadows and a figure emerges, and Victor makes himself known. Matthias can tell he’s kindred (Sense the Unseen), and Victor indicates that several heavily armed figures entered the tunnels just minutes before. Matthias thanks him and follows after them.

Alice, Adisa, Catherine and Tony continue into the tunnels, when they are beset by feelings of deep hunger. Alice realizes this is the effect of blood sorcery, perhaps built into the tunnel itself.

They discuss waiting for Matthias, and Tony decides to run back and see if he can spot him.

Tony darts back (Celerity), and notices as he passes them a squad of heavily armed police, wearing goggles but no lights, who are startled. He decides to try to lure them into a side chamber, and approaches them with Awe. They are having none of it, and several of them fire their rifles. Tony sustains heavy damage.

Everyone else in the tunnels hears this. Adisa charges forward. Alice and Catherine hurriedly sneak after her. Matthias activates Arms of Ahiram and approaches.

Matthias is able to observe them before they see him, and he sees four humans dressed for tactical combat; one who is armed with a sword instead, and a sixth figure that seems to be a Thin-Blood, unarmed.

Tony darts back into the shadows (Cloak of Shadows), desperately hoping that their coterie comes in clutch.

Matthias splits the tendrils into five, and tries to throw the five humans at the vampire, but the tactical suited ones are merely distracted by the shadows. The one with the sword gets raised and thrown, and tumbles onto the vampire, both falling over. Matthias frenzies, compelled to harm and destroy these interlopers, furious that the thin-blood would protect themselves with five fucking *humans*.

Adisa charges in and jumps on the back of one of the riflemen. She knocks the rifle out of his hand, and tears at his armor as he tries to reach for his sidearm.

Alice succumbs to her own compulsion of Tremere-style perfectionism. She approaches and spits venomous vitae (Scorpion’s Touch) at the Thin-Blood, who sees it just in time and drops to the ground to dodge it. She notices (See the Unseen) Tony hiding in the shadows.

Tony darts forward and grabs one of the riflemen and ducks back into the shadows, devouring him as he uses him as a human shield. (Messy Crit) Tony drains him dry.

Matthias splits his shadow arms into two; one grasps the thin-blood and hoists it in front of Alice’s face. The other arm creeps towards what seems like the officer, but the officer holds something forth and speaks strange words, and the shadow arm dissipates into nothing.

Adisa wrestles away the sidearm, only to have the man with the sword stab her through the back.

Catherine comes forward, and commands “Drop it!” (Compel). The man drops the sword.

Alice spits again right into the thin-blood’s face, and the Thin-Blood screams as her face bubbles and boils.

Tony is overwhelmed by the feeding and guilt, but swears they can see a towering shadow behind Alice. Tony decides to use the moment of having just killed one of their number to try to scare the others. “I will rip your throat out too, if you don’t freaking stop!”

The officer pulls his rifle up, and calls out to his remaining men. “They’re making threats! We have them on the back foot.” He fires three rounds straight into Tony’s chest. [Tony is one hit away from going down].

Matthias maintains his hold on the thin-blood.

Adisa has disarmed and brought the guy she was engaged with prone.

Alice feels a rush of air as something lunges over her. A monstrous being, bestial (but not a werewolf) grabs the thin-blood’s leg and bends it until the knee snaps the wrong way. With the other hand it grabs one of the riflemen’s heads and rips it straight off.

Lady Catherine tries to Mesmerize the man who dropped the sword, but he appears to be able to resist it.

Alice spits over Catherine’s shoulder and hits the man in the eyes. He screams in pain and drops to the ground, clutching at his face.

Tony retreats again and uses the power of the blood to recover slightly.

Matthias tries a tug-of-war with the thin-blood, but this aggravates the beast, who tugs back, hard. Matthias retains grip on a leg, but the remainder of the thin-blood is thrown across the width of the tunnel. Matthias tries again to grasp at the officer, but again the arm dissipates.

Alice calls to Catherine “tell them to stop!”. Catherine stands tall and orders the officer, but the others more generally. “Lower your arms. *Now*!”

The officer complies. The beast uses the opportunity to grab him by the torso with one hand, the legs with the other, and twists the man apart. It then leaps away and returns down the tunnel.

Adisa binds the man she’s brought down, and Catherine goes to tend to Tony. Matthias feeds on the man with the burning eyes.

Alice and Matthias then approach the thin-blood. Alice: “Who are you? What is your purpose?”

The thin-blood is clearly in pain. “You fucking monster. Just put me out of my misery.”

The thin-blood shuts up when Alice repeats the question.

Matthias tries. “If you explain why you were sent to kill us, I’ll allow you a swift death. Otherwise it will be slow.”

Thin-blood: “An end is all I ask for. Quicker would be better.”

“I was assigned to this unit as part of the, you know, SO13 active unit under Paul Richards; he was the one that the *thing* tore apart.”

Matthias: “You work for the human?”

Thin-blood: “I’m not keen on the disease I carry.”

Alice: “What’s your name?”

Gabrielle: “Gabrielle.”

Matthias: “What is the SO13?”

Gabrielle: “It’s the Metropolitan Anti-Terrorism unit. I’m part of the ECTU; the Extraordinary Counter-Terrorism, you know?”

Matthias: “Oh, they *were* cops. Oh shit.” He is intent on ripping this thin-blood apart the moment their interrogation is over.

arc.title: Session 14: Cleaning Up
arc.text:
Catherine looks around: “Where’s my puppet? Did you see her?”

Matthias: “Briefly, on my way down. I grabbed a mop and had tried to walk past them.”

Catherine leaves Gabrielle to Matthias to be torn to shreds, heads over to the remaining human and interrogates him.

Catherine’s eyes turn red and yellow, bestial. “How did you know we were down here?”

Adisa is standing a little ways off: she’s got his rifle and sidearm, a couple knives, several wooden stakes, and is pouring out what seems to be holy water onto the ground. “These people came *prepared*.”

Catherine: “How the *fuck* did you know about us?”

Man: “We got a call from the officers monitoring on the street. They had an informant.”

Catherine: “I *see*. That *whore*. Did you catch what the informant looked like?”

Man: “I assume it was the lady standing with them when we arrived.”

Catherine: “Matthias? Feel like going up to the street with me? I feel like ripping heads.” She grabs the sidearm from Adisa, and gives her the knife. Catherine feels no compunction about killing the humans, given that the Masquerade has been breached.

Matthias is feeling rough but joins Adisa and Catherine heading back. When they get to the station, Victor asks if they’re leaving and whether he can come with. He agrees to “protect from the rear”.

They try to approach stealthily but unsuccessfully; the female officer hears something and says, “Sounds like they’re coming back up. Hopefully they got those terrorists.” There’s a pause, and then they can hear Claire say, “That’s not them. We need to run.”

Catherine bolts up the stairs, and Adisa goes up even faster, connecting with the male officer who’s turning the corner at the same time. He gets a knife in the gut, and Adisa’s claws grip his throat.

Catherine reaches the top of the stairs shortly after, tries to aim past Adisa and shoot to maim the female officer. She misses, and becomes enraged. [Dominance compulsion]

Catherine: “Claire! Get your ass over here, *now*.” (Dominate) She turns to Matthias. “Restrain these fucks.” [Harm compulsion]

Matthias doesn’t even hear her, but brings forth the arms of shadow (Arms of Ahiram) and grapples the one Adisa is holding up into unconsciousness.

Catherine storms forward, tries to smack the female officer with the butt of her pistol. Her moves are telegraphed, and the officer uses her baton to make it a glancing blow, and swings back. The baton cracks into the jaw, dislocating it, but Catherine’s fortitude keeps it from causing further damage. (Toughness)

Claire is glassy-eyed, has turned and is walking back.

Matthias sends the shadow arms over towards the female officer. One wraps around her right leg and pulls her knee to the pavement. She struggles to stay upright.

Catherine ignores the pain, pops her jaw back into place. She catches the officer’s gaze. “Kneel.” (Mesmerize) The woman kneels and bows, chin up to attempt to maintain eye contact.

Adisa calls out. “I think we’re clear.” Victor runs up and runs away.

Catherine slaps Claire, knocking her to the side. Claire whimpers. Catherine slaps her repeatedly, Claire trying and failing to raise an arm in defense. Adisa turns her back, Matthias leaves Catherine to her pet human.

Catherine: “I gave you a gift. I gave you the chance to serve me, and possibly become one of us, and you *betray* me? How long? And is my banker a part of this scheme? *Answer me*.”

Claire’s eyes are full of terror. “I had no idea. I had no idea they were going to do that and I didn’t know what to do. I’m sorry.”

Catherine: “The penalty for your betrayal is death.” She asks Adisa for the knife, who gives it up against her better judgment, and Catherine walks up to Claire again, who has burst in to tears and is gasping from shock and feelings of powerlessness, hopelessness.

“She risked the Masquerade,” and Catherine stabs Claire to death. Claire gives out a sharp cry before the moans stop. [Catherine loses 1 humanity]

Looking back on this, Catherine will recognize that she believed Claire’s ignorance, and was fueled by her compulsions. But nothing will undo this.

Matthias has found and killed the police dog, kills the female officer, and takes some time to turn the officer’s corpses to ash (Ashes to Ashes). He brings the dog body down to the station, reawakens it (Awaken the Homuncular Servant), names it Carlo.

Catherine carries Claire down to the station, finds a stretch in the tunnel where she can make a mound burial for Claire. She searched Claire, took her purse which has a flip phone, some contacts in there, and her ID card, some cash and cards.

Matthias tries to get the dog to follow a scent, and they follow Carlo back to where they had been ambushed. The man they were interrogating was gone, and Alice and Tony are missing as well.

Matthias gets hungrier.

They push ahead, following Carlo, and they come upon a train that has been stalled on the tracks. They follow it, passing a tunnel on the right, and continue past until Carlo leads them to a carriage car, windows broken and some partially blocked. Catherine moves towards the entrance, sees the door hanging on its hinges and the mess inside, and realizes that this must be the nest of the creature that interfered in the attack earlier. She relays this to the others, and they decide to leave it alone and check out the tunnel they passed.

They eventually get close to another derelict platform, and Carlo perks up. They do a double-take and see a woman sitting on the platform.

[Image: Untitled 2.png](campaign/assets/gm/fall-of-london-the-story-so-far-untitled-2.webp)

Catherine calls over to her. “Is this the entrance to get to Richard de Worde?”

The woman immediately shifts from carefree to jumping to her feet and backing away. “Please, please don’t hurt me!”

Matthias uses See the Unseen, recognizes hers as kindred, clanless but not thin-blood, and that she was or is attempting to make herself invisible. She’s not as scared as she’s making herself out to be.

Catherine: “We intend you no harm.”

Matthias directs Carlo ahead. “I think this may be a trap.”

Catherine: “Look sister, we mean you no harm, we’re just trying to find this Nosferatu, he supposedly has something for us. I’m going to reach into this bag, and it’s not a weapon,” she pulls out a necklace, “it’s something for you if you’ll show us where to find him.”

The woman looks warily, “He doesn’t like strangers, he’s really shy. But if he likes you, he’s the best guy in the world. He told me to keep an eye on you.”

Catherine: “Okay, but we need to meet with him. He’s got something we need. I have some information I’m willing to trade with him. He likes information, right?”

Woman: “He loves it and I like the jewelry. You have more of it?”

Catherine: “I have more I can give you once we’ve found him.”

Woman: “I guess… I guess I can take you to a spot and then have him meet you there. It would be, like, an entryway. And then I’ll go find him.”

Matthias uses Premonition, tries to get a read (7 successes!), he can tell that the woman is largely telling the truth, *except* for the part about leading them *to* Richard de Worde. She has no intention of bringing you to him.

Matthias: “Yes, you can get Richard for us. Our mistress, Queen Anne, will be very pleased.” He’s trying to subtly indicate what’s up to the others without saying anything directly.

Woman: “Ok, well, follow me.” And she walks confidently down the tunnels.

They follow the tunnels for a bit, then open a door and go through some maintenance hallways that open into corridors with grating and huge pipes. Eventually more hallways and a staircase down, and another door. The woman opens it up and inside is a large maintenance room; piled pipes block the rear door, lockers line the walls, and chalk and blood outlines indicate that some sort of ritual had been performed here.

Matthias, Adisa, and Catherine have all reached 3 hunger.

Woman: “Well, this is where de Worde will meet you. I’ll tell him the emissaries of Queen Anne are here to see him. Can I see the necklace?”

Matthias: “No!”

Catherine: “I would feel better if you went and got him, first.”

Woman: “You said the *other* pieces would be for when I got him. Half now, half later.”

Catherine: “What assurance do I have?”

Woman: “That’s why you’re only giving me half.”

Catherine: “Fine.” She breaks the necklace she’s holding in half. She sees there’s only one unobstructed way out, which is the way they came in.

Woman: “You give me both halves, like we agreed; I’ll get you de Worde, like we agreed; and then you’ll give me the other jewelry, like we agreed.”

Catherine steps forward as if to give it to her, then brushes her finger against the woman’s cheek. (Entrancement, Messy Crit).

Catherine’s hungry and irritated and this pipsqueak of a girl is trying to gatekeep *de Worde*. Richard had been a confidant of Mithras for *centuries* before this girl existed. And Catherine’s force of personality causes the woman to just crumble.

Catherine: “Now there, wouldn’t you like to take us to de Worde?”

Woman: “You know, I would do anything to see you happy. I can’t wait for him to meet you. I’m sure he’ll love you like he loves me. He’s been so good to me and I think you’ll really appreciate him.”

The woman, who they learn is named Rea, leads them on for another half hour or so, until they get to something like a bunker, with a wheeled vault door. Rea opens it and brings them into the quarters of Richard de Worde.

arc.title: Session 15: Bunker 788
arc.text:
Catherine, Adisa, and Matthias gain another hunger (now at 4).

While Adisa, Matthias, and Catherine leave, Tony is trying to wrap up his injuries. He notices something and retreats to the shadows in time to see a bestial form grab Alice and drag her off.

Cautiously, Tony follows it at a distance, as Alice struggles and fails to free herself. Eventually it comes up to a vault door, which it turns to open. Tony gets a glimpse of the room inside before the door is closed behind.

Inside the room, the monstrous creature walks through, pulls a rug back, and shifts a 15-foot diameter steel lid. There’s a concrete pit about 20-feet deep, and it throws Alice down.

Alice: “Wait! I think I know who you are! You don’t need to fear me! I have some questions for you!”

The creature makes an unintelligible response as it pulls the lid back over the pit.

Alice feels her stomach drop, and her hunger goes to 4.

Tony hides in the shadows, and sees the creature emerge from the room. It sniffs, but decides against and moves away. Once it’s far enough Tony enters the vault.

The interior looks like an auditorium-style 1940s war office. Three levels, desks, desk lamps, filing cabinets, with stacks of paper, rotary phones, train schedules posted that are several decades out of date.

Tony has a brief flashback to a woman, graceful but determined, who walks up to him and slaps him hard across the face, knocking him down. Tony jumps up, fists up instinctively, but the woman disappeared, reappearing behind him and pulling him towards her. “My sire will be so pleased with you,” she says, and she sinks her teeth into Tony.

Tony comes back to the present and starts looking around, when he hears Alice. “Anyone hear me?!” The sound is muffled, coming from under the floorboards. It takes Tony ten minutes to discover the lid under the carpet, and just then hears the vault door opening again.

sections.title: A memory from the 11th century
sections.text:
It’s a mithraeum. Torch lit, ghoul servants. Mithras seats himself. Roger de Camden follows. Someone brings in a young man, in a stupor. Roger holds the young man’s wrists over Mithras’ chalice, and bleeds him into the chalice until the youth expires.

Mithras: “I thank you for joining this ritual. This mortal has proven worthy of the blooding, with his unrelenting service to the cult. And we show our gratitude by giving him the gift of the blood.

Catherine sees that de Camden is skeptical that the ritual will work.

Mithras looks to Catherine, and invites her to come forward to add her blood. She obeys.

Alice comes forward next, then Tony, each adding their blood to blend. Some of the blood pours over the young man’s face, his body cradled by Mithras. Suddenly his eyes shoot open and he starts thrashing and trying to get away. His look of desperation is extinguished as Mithras crushes his trachea. Mithras stands abruptly, dropping the body, and says, “I appreciate what you have given. We will resume this at a later date. You are dismissed.”

As their senses return to the present, Catherine wakes on a lovely antique sedan inside the bunker office. Rea leans against a desk across from her, and a Nosferatu, his face looking sloughed off, is dressed sharply in an old suit and is seated beside Rea. The hunger is like a gut punch.

Tony and Alice awaken in pure darkness, sensing each other’s presence.

Tony: “Hello?”

Alice: “Is that Tony?”

Tony: “Where are you?”

Tony shuffles over until he can feel Alice’s hand on the floor.

Alice: “How did you get here?”

Tony explains what he saw, including the room above.

Catherine: “Richard de Worde, I presume?”

de Worde: “The one and only. You were seeking me out?”

Catherine: “I’m quite parched. Do you happen to have any sustenance I could partake of?”

de Worde: “I might. Who did you come with?”

Catherine: “Well, there was Matthias…”

de Worde: “Ah, the Puttanesca. I returned him to his family. I owed them a debt they can now consider paid.”

Catherine: “…then there was Alice, and Tony, and Adisa.”

de Worde: “I believe I have two of those three. The Banu Hakim put up a bit of a fight; unwisely, shall we say?”

Catherine: “So she is no longer in the world?”

de Worde: “There is something of her in me.”

Catherine: “I have come prepared to make an exchange.”

de Worde: “You were asking about sustenance.” He stands and walks across the room, pulls back the carpet and then shifts the steel lid. The light, though dim, blinds Alice and Tony below. “I believe these are yours.”

Catherine looks down. “They are my companions, sir.”

Rea tosses a rope ladder down, and Alice and Tony climb up.

de Worde gestures. “Please, take a seat.”

Alice looks around suspiciously, and then finds a chair.

de Worde resumes his seat. “Rea, bring in the mortal we had found with them. Our guests must be famished.” Rea returns with the paramilitary captive. de Worde stands and walks behind the man. “The hunger that drives us, can be quite distressing. He bites into the man’s neck and in a mere few seconds, drains him completely dry, the body shriveling. (Brutal Feed) There’s nothing left for anyone else. Hunger surges in Tony.

Alice takes superficial willpower damage and Tony takes aggravated willpower damage (Dementation). Catherine clocks the mind games that de Worde is playing with them; this is a power play.

de Worde looks around and sees the stress. “Oh, my apologies. It seems this is not enough to go around. Perhaps we’ll be able to find something else soon. What brings you here?”

Catherine: “Respectfully, stop with the fucking games and let’s get down to business.”

de Worde: “It seems you must be taught respect.” (Coax the Bestial Temper) [Catherine is forced to make a frenzy roll, successfully resists it - 5 successes]

Catherine can feel de Worde trying to nudge her over the edge, and by sheer force of will she resists it. “We came here to do *business*. I brought something in exchange. Your games are uncalled for. Is this how you treat guests? Are you not civilized enough?”

de Worde: “I don’t have guests, I have victims. I’ve been keeping an eye on you. You seem to be in league with Mithras, trying to revive him. Bring him back to this ‘life’ or whatever you wish to call it.”

Catherine: “So you are an enemy of Mithras.”

de Worde: “Enemy implies hostility. This is rational. Can you imagine a millenia-old vampire ruling the modern world? I wish to prevent chaos. I wish to avoid the Beckoning. I am here for my welfare.”

Alice: “You do not welcome the coming of our Lord? What do you have to fear from him?”

de Worde turns to Alice. “All these years and still his pup, still his pet. I’ve known Mithras for *centuries* longer than you, Heliodramus.”

Alice: “You have nothing to fear if you are his devoted; he loves you as much as he loves the rest of us.”

de Worde: “He loves me as much as he loves you, which is not at all. He has no capacity for love.”

Alice: “Why do you say that?”

de Worde: “Do any of us? Love is one of the first things to go.”

Catherine: “Love is a human emotion. I get what you’re saying, but we are his Heralds. We have a duty.”

de Worde: “You seek his dagger. That, and sustenance. My sorcery has that effect on people.”

Catherine: “I will not lie; I am parched, but I have something you might like in exchange; I have information on Queen Anne.”

de Worde: “You are decades late. I have no care as to what happens in London above.”

Alice: “You’re not going to stay safe here forever.”

de Worde: “It is my only option.”

Alice: “There is strength in numbers. You could join with us.”

Catherine: “It’s already clear, he is not.”

de Worde: “I was born in the 11th century. The beckoning calls to me. I will not seek it. I have hidden myself away. Apparently I have not sufficiently disincentivized visitors. But I will cut you a deal. You will leave without the dagger. And I will allow you to quench your thirst.”

Alice realizes it’s the ceremonial dagger that’s been powering the blood sorcery that has been driving their hunger.

Alice: “You will be left here alone. I see how the dagger serves your purpose. Is that what you really want?”

Catherine: “He does have someone.” She nods at Rea. “And I think that monster we saw.”

de Worde: “You met my Guardian. And you know Rea. I’m not alone, and I have ways of attending to my needs.”

They feel the pressure of Dementation again.

Catherine: “Alice, let’s stop trying to reason with him. Let’s count it as a loss right now.”

Alice: “You don’t understand. He’s using the dagger for his own purposes.”

Catherine: “Isn’t that what Mithras will do? Isn’t it freeing that Mithras *isn’t* here and we can do what we want?”

Alice: “How can you say such a thing?!”

Catherine: “The old ways are gone. We’re in a new era. If we bring someone back from the old era, who’s to say he’s not going to bring the room down on us?”

Alice jumps from her seat. “How *dare* you say such a thing? If I knew this would come out of your mouth, I would have, I would have…”

de Worde claps, slowly. “The Ventrue at least understands the situation. And our Tremere understands why I cannot give the dagger to you. Yes, it is somewhere in my kingdom but the underworld is far too vast for you to dig through everything. So I give you the best of luck in your search, and I bid you adieu.” And he vanishes right in front of their eyes. (Vanish) Rea, too, seems to be missing.

Tony: “We’re going to have to reconvene. Shit’s piling up.”

Catherine: “Let’s get out of here.”

Alice starts desperately searching around the room for the dagger. She’s half-starved, and shocked.

Catherine opens the vault door and makes to leave.

Behind one of the paintings, Alice finds a safe. Tony comes over and manages to get it open, ignoring the desperate hunger in his gut. There’s a number of brown paper folders inside, including several with their names. The information is from the 1940s: names, contacts, feeding habits, when they were typically out for the night. There are photographs, including one of Angelique and Catherine in a supposedly private rendezvous. Catherine walks over and snatches it, puts it in her purse.

Tony is looking through his folder, and sees that his sire is indicated as being Saeth, whose sire is Gwenllian ferch Arwyn.

Alice gives Tony the stack of papers she had; she isn’t interested in these at this moment, but one paper strikes her, it has a single type-written line on it. “The heralds lair lies unprotected. They are weak but not broken.”

Alice finds a ribbon and begins using her blood to Illuminate the Trail of Prey on both de Worde and Rea. She sees Catherine move to stop her, and holds up a finger. “Don’t.”

Catherine: “We can’t go after them *now*. We are trapped in his lair.”

Alice: “I need to finish this.”

Catherine: “Fine. I’m leaving. Tony, you can stay or follow, but this is a death trap, and I need sustenance.” Tony follows.

Alice completes the ritual, sees that they exited through a side door that presumably goes deeper into the lair. She knows that this will hold for one night, and then she follows the others back.

As Catherine and Tony are walking, before Alice has caught up, Catherine assures Tony: “I *am* loyal to Mithras, but sometimes the appearance of disloyalty can mean the difference between success and failure.”

Tony feels that Catherine is tricky, schemes within schemes, and can’t help feeling that this is another scheme.

Catherine tries to lead them back, but Tony catches her taking a wrong turn and takes over with directions.

They exit the station, and split up to go feed.

Catherine’s beast takes control as she hunts, and it heads to a red light district and collects several streetwalkers to join her. It’s not ideal or her preferred prey, but it’s enough to take the edge off and leave her a little less desperate before going back to the haven.

Tony’s first impulse is to find a blood bank or a hospice home but instead finds himself weaving through alleys. A corpse beckons, and though it is not a fresh kill, and the blood is rancid, it is enough to help Tony move back towards the haven.

Alice is looking to feed, but more so is looking for validation. Having a true apostate in Richard de Worde, and another potential apostate in Lady Catherine, is deeply distressing, and she looks to reestablish the cultic hierarchy.

She heads back to the occult shop from earlier. The same young woman (Laila) is there as a clerk. Alice feeds on her, and then takes time teaching her the first step, Corax the Raven, in the Seven steps to the Sun. The woman is enthralled by Alice, and fascinated by the teachings. They arrange a time for Alice to return.

They return to the haven, and find Matthias outside, in an argument or discussion with someone from Elysium: Calogero Puttanesca.

Catherine sees Alice and tells her: “I know you think I’m turning on Mithras. I’m not. I just needed us to get the fuck out of there.” She walks inside without waiting for a response.

Alice has her speak to the hand, ignores her and goes inside.

arc.title: Session 16: Out of the Frying Pan
arc.text:
Matthias’ body has been functioning in the world, but his consciousness seemingly clicks back into place and he’s in Calogero’s limousine. He’s been watching Matthias. “Ah, you’re back.”

Matthias: “Don’t know where I went.”

Calogero: “I received word from the Nosferatu that I was to come pick you up from outside an underground station. What were you doing?”

Matthias: “Well, I was looking for a Nosferatu, and then I woke up here.”

Calogero: “It seems your company was undesired.”

Matthias: “It generally is.”

Calogero: “Well, regardless I will have to thank him for the opportunity to congratulate you in person. I here you had something to do with our late seneschal’s passing.”

Matthias isn’t sure they did in fact kill Valerius, but he nods and says, “I had a small part to play.”

Calogero: “Well between that and whatever it was that happened at Elysium — I was fortunate to have made an exit earlier — it seems there are openings to be made. Not merely for primogen of the Hecata, but perhaps, for prince. I have reached out to the justicar, Juliet Parr, about the possibility. Queen Anne may perhaps not be the leader we need in these times.”

Matthias: “I’m shocked, *shocked*. Of *course* she’s not the leader we need; any goat can see that.”

Calogero: “Well, seeing it, and making it effected are distinct.”

Matthias: “I’ve been awake for a week and already her rule is shattering.”

Calogero: “In past months I’ve come into something that I believe will allow for leverage.” He indicates the empty seat to his left, and Matthias’ *See the Unseen* comes into focus. The spirit of a haughty woman whispers in his ear. “A ventrue once owed me a great boon, and met her final death before she could make good. I have been availing myself of her services in learning some of the more underhanded secrets of the Ventrue.”

“You should check in with Lady Scarlet and assure her of whatever it is that it seems you’ve done. I’m sure she is delighted at the recent opening. Only a fool could miss that she was being groomed for higher office, and I’m sure the keeper of Elysium, Regina Blake, is deeply relieved that Scarlet will be poised for the seneschal’s position and not her own. But either warrant a connection, to remain on their good side until the justicar can weigh in.”

Matthias: “Smiley and polite until it’s time not to be.”

The car pulls up and Matthias sees Alice storm into the building with Lady Catherine following at a remove.

Catherine: “You missed a complete shitshow.”

Matthias: “I’m sorry about that; no idea what happened. Woke up in a limo, don’t even remember going to sleep.”

Catherine: “Well, that asshole said his debt to your family is paid.”

Matthias: “Didn’t know he owed, but glad he’s keeping up on his bills. Did you get any useful information?”

Catherine: “He’s a total dick and isn’t to be trusted. He’s got the dagger, and is using it for some type of blood rituals. Remember that feeling in the tunnels?”

Matthias: “Felt pretty hungry pretty quick.”

Catherine: “That was him. We were his victims, not his guests. My self-preservation impulse kicked in, I said what I thought he wanted to hear to get us out, but now Alice thinks I’m an apostate.”

Matthias: “Apostate? Not contagious, I hope.”

Catherine: “She’ll come back to reason. She takes our lord’s service a bit too seriously.”

Matthias: “Enthusiastic.”

Catherine: “Fucking fanatic.”

Matthias: “Do we know how to deal with his sorcery?”

Catherine: “Well, de Worde is not wanting to answer the beckoning. He’s not going to give the dagger up.”

They catch up on Alice’s ritual, on Valerius’ death, and Matthias makes a plan to learn more about the underground, making some counter-sorcery.

They walk inside the haven. Tony is already there, and is in a shouting match with Alice over Ferhat.

Catherine side-steps them and finds Ollie. He tells her the deed is done, evidence cleaned up as best as possible. She pulls a ring out for him, puts it on his finger, and draws him into the bedroom.

Matthias gets some bagged blood and takes over the study and after some research, sends a message out to his retainer to pull schematics for a section of the underground.

Alice storms in and Matthias convinces her to assist with coming up with a plan to resist the magic hunger underground. She does some research and finds reason to believe there are some artifacts that could do this.

Alice also reaches out to Oskar Anasov asking for a way to reach Gwenllian Arwyn.

Lady Catherine calls Lady Scarlet, but receives a message. “This number cannot receive calls.” She calls Darius.

Darius: “Who is this?”

Catherine: “Lady Catherine.”

Darius: “Oh, thank goodness.”

Catherine: “I’m trying to get a message to Queen Anne. The mission she had us undertake has been completed.”

Darius: “I don’t have a direct channel to her. She’s… did you not hear?”

Catherine: “I heard about the attack on Elysium.”

Darius: “Yes; there’s a number of kindred dead. The sheriff of north London is gone, a number of other folks. I would guess that connecting through Valerius, or Regina Blake, or Lady Scarlet, would make the most sense.

Catherine: “Valerius went up in a bomb.”

Darius: “The humans took him, too?”

Catherine: “Yes.”

Darius: “This… is far more severe than I imagined. Well, Regina has a club, called The Trunk, that I don’t see her ever leaving. Otherwise Lady Scarlet…”

Catherine: “I tried calling her and she’s not receiving.”

Darius: “I have a dead drop. I’ll relay your message.” He hangs up.

sections.title: Sunday
sections.text:
The next night…

Matthias’ retainer has left a thick envelope. The thin paper unfolds into large spreads, with various sections of the tunnels for an area about a mile and a half in diameter. The area above where they were seems mostly commercial and light industrial buildings. A public park sits atop another section. There are multiple points of entry; too many to manage.

The larger passageways are clear. Doors and ladders are less clear.

Catherine and Matthias talk about trying to plug entrances, siege him, flush him out, and ultimately that seems futile; there’s too many. They identify several other viable entrances to get back to the bunker.

Catherine: “What if the dagger isn’t hidden? What if it’s on him? How the hell are we to take him down? We still have some of the toys you took from Anne.”

Matthias: “I’m not sure my shotgun and bulletproof vest is going to mean a whole lot since he was able to put the whammy on me without me even walking through the door, and he seemed more than a match for the three of you.

Catherine: “Four; three of us survived. Is there a way we could mess with his ritual? Cause it to backfire?”

Alice enters. She met with Laila, they have necklaces for everyone that she cautiously believes may counteract the effects.

Catherine: “I’m going to go to The Trunk. Maybe Regina or someone else knows something that can gives us an edge against de Worde.”

They take a cab over, and they aren’t asked for IDs, just get a stamp. The dance floor is crowded, there’s a drag show on stage, and at one of the balconies is an ornate couch. Regina is seated, reigning, with a young man’s head in her lap being stroked, and a woman kneeling in front of her, Regina cupping her chin in her hand, speaking.

Regina: “Welcome, and drink. My domain is your domain tonight. Come and chat once you’ve had your fill.”

Alice finds a young man and brings him over to her. She asks him about what brought him, he says he likes the vibes, his housemate is one of the performers. Doesn’t always remember his nights here. He points out some of the people, and highlights Regina, commenting that she’s *not* the owner, but she’s the queen of this place; always here, always has people hanging on her every word. That he would love to get close to her. His name’s Malik. Alice asks about rumors, and he said there were some disappearances that some thought were tied to human trafficking, but that club management really was proactive and said they’d put in safeguards and there hasn’t been any issues for the past year or so.

Matthias is at the bar ignoring them, communicating with Carlo, the undead puppy, who he left in an alley outside. *Find and kill a rat for me*.

Catherine has found four or five people to fawn over her in one of the booths tucked away.

Malik is describing blissed-out experiences, sanctioned and unsanctioned, and Alice asks what he means. He brings her upstairs, past Catherine, over to some diwaniya-style couches. There’s a woman cradling a man’s body, kissing or possibly feeding from him. Malik walks past and over to a couple holding hands on a sedan. He introduces them as Tibor and Lila, that they have had trysts in the past and that their kisses are electric. Alice sees immediately that they are kindred, probably Gangrel.

Carlo reports to Matthias that there are one, two, many…. many rats. Matthias heads back and collects the corpses to begin resurrecting a rat surveillance army.

Catherine finally extricates herself and presents to Regina. “I was trying to get in touch with the prince, I heard there was bad news.”

Regina motions for her hangers-on to hang back, and rises. “We can speak in my office.” She leads Catherine through a curtain and down a hallway, through another curtain and door into a modest office with dim lighting. There’s filing cabinets and a desk, and a giant mural of a vagina. She sits at her desk and gestures to the seat in front of her. “So you haven’t heard from her, either.”

Catherine: “I have not.”

Regina: “I’ve never had an Elysium go south like that before. I wouldn’t be surprised if I was replaced at court. I have no idea who those people were; it’s amazing that I was able to escape.”

Catherine: “They were human?”

Regina: “Yes, but they fought with fire, they, they knew what they were doing.”

Catherine explains about the team they encountered in the tunnels, and describes some of the other information, but not its provenance.”

Regina: “I think she’s gone to ground and is waiting to make sure things are secure before making announcements. But I haven’t had any word. Someone picked up my retainer a couple nights ago on drunk & disorderly and possession of narcotics, and that’s who I’d usually use as a go-between in situations like this. Trenton is being held at Bishopsgate; if you were able to get him out, I would owe you a boon.”

Catherine: “Well, I’m not sure I can do that. I just wanted to relay to Queen Anne that the mission she had entrusted me with was accomplished.”

Regina: “It is near-certain that I will hear from her in the next day or two. I can relay that information. I can’t promise that I will be Keeper after.”

Catherine: “It’s not your fault, Gina. You didn’t invite them in.”

Regina: “Let’s be clear; if you were prince you would do the same. Regardless, if you are even able to get me information about Trenton’s wellbeing, I would owe you a minor boon; major if he’s returned to me safely.”

Catherine: “I will find them. On another note, do you know how I could get ahold of the justicar?”

Regina: “That is someone I can get ahold of. How should she contact you?”

Catherine gives her number.

Regina: “Great, I’ll be in touch.”

arc.title: Session 17 - Plans Within Plans
arc.text:
Sunday, continued

Upon getting back to the haven, there’s a car waiting. Matthias enters with the undead rats and dog, and then comes into the haven and gives Tony a card, only to return to the car and leave for somewhere. The card greets Tony as sibling, and indicates a meat-packing plant where he can meet Chun Hei.

They arrive, it’s dark but there are some people by the warehouse and some lights in the offices. Catherine strides forward towards the warehouse, taps the man standing outside on the shoulding. “I’m looking for Chun Hei. She never specified a time, but it’s urgent.”

Goon: “Who’s asking?”

Tony: “Her sibling.”

Catherine: “And friends of her sibling.” With effort, Catherine *Mesmerizes* the man. *Take us to Chun Hei*. He calls up to three others on a steel balcony.

Alice recognizes that these goons are Brujah ghouls.

They come back, confirm that they’re ok to bring the coterie in, and lead them to Chun Hei.

[my recording failed here, so a brief summary from memory]

Chun Hei indicates that they were approached by Oskar Anasov, was told to reach out to Alice. She made the connection from Elysium, and reached out to Tony instead. She notes how she and Tony are in a similar place: with Zawadi, her sire, dead, and Saeth, Tony’s sire, also dead.

sections.title: Bishopsgate
sections.text:
Catherine heads to Bishopsgate, enters through the main public entrance. Despite being 4am, there are a half dozen people sitting around in the lobby, one officer at the reception desk, and another sitting behind.

Catherine approaches the receptionist. “Darling.”

Receptionist: “Do you have a case number?”

Catherine: “I’m looking for Trenton? Trenton Adebayo?”

She types the name, and searches. “And your business with him is?

Catherine: “I’m his lover.”

Receptionist: “Your business with him *here*, I mean.”

Catherine: “Well, his partner asked me to get him out of here. It’s something of an open relationship.” Catherine is using her full charm, but not supplementing it with any vampiric powers in this place.

More typing, then. “Bail is £50. Please sign this form.”

Finally, Trenton comes out.

Catherine: “Trenton, darling! Regina wants to see you again.”

His eyes shift from confusion to reassurance, and they walk out of the prison. He explains he was in for drunk & disorderly, which was escalated to assaulting an officer. He’s visibly shaking from not having had Regina’s blood.

They head back to the Trunk. Regina is overjoyed.

Catherine explains their goal in trying to find Arwyn, asks if Regina can relay a message to her.

Regina: “This wouldn’t happen to have anything with the red list, would it?”

Catherine assures her it does not. The message to be relayed is: “The heralds of Mithras seek the property that is theirs. Will you comply? And will you help with de Worde?”

Regina asks for two days, at which point she will either have succeeded and the boon will be considered discharged, or she will provide an update.

sections.title: Gala at the British Museum
sections.text:
The place is quite busy, and the group splits up to explore. Matthias activates Share the Senses, targeting Catherine. There are socialites, academics, young professionals, and others.

Oliver and Catherine head to the Roman Empire gallery. Catherine is looking around for Arwyn. She doesn’t see her, but she does notice a tall Sikh man who appears to be an officer. Then she recognizes some of the insignia on his breast: Metropolitan Anti-Terrorism, and ECTU.

He’s observant but doesn’t seem to be on-duty, is engaged in conversation.

Matthias has also entered the gallery, looking at the busts, and then he stumbles across an exhibit which is clearly the Phrygian cap they seek. He clocks it for later. Someone brushes against him and he turns to see several people in a tour group, led by none other than Gwenllian ferch Arwyn.

sections.title: Memorium
sections.text:
Immediately their senses are thrown disorientingly into the past. They are in Roman London, and the Ventrue Marcus Verus is questioning his childe about the status of the construction for the mithraeum; a cultic center for the worship of Mithras.

The scene shifts, and Verus stands before a god of light, glowing like the sun. It is Mithras himself.

Mithras speaks. “Who do you love more than me?”

Verus denies that there is any. Mithras does not accept this answer, and repeats the question.

Verus folds, explains that his childe, Arcadius, holds a deeper place in his heart.

Mithras accepts the honestly, and hands the cap to Verus. “I am entrusting this to you, my beloved servant. If there is ever a question of saving yourself, or this cap, you must choose the cap.”

Verus accepts and bows low.

A third vision; Verus and Mithras stand, and you see through the eyes of Arwyn.

Mithras is sending Verus abroad, and has selected Arwyn to be the protector of the cap in his stead.

Matthias feels a wave of anxiety; wants to pass off the hot potato.

Catherine wonders if there is some connection between the cap and resolving the conflict with one’s beast.

Mithras: “Lord Verus serves me well, but I require him elsewhere. I’ve chosen you, Arwyn, among all my faithful, to take his holy charge from him. I acknowledge you may be reticent, that it may seem a symbol of your conqueror. Take it instead as a symbol of your god.”

Arwyn rages at having been subjugated twice; first as a Briton, and second when losing her mortality. But she is also devout, and she accepts.

Their senses return to the present.

Catherine’s eyes dart around, and they land on Arwyn across the room. She takes Oliver by the arm and strides towards her.

Matthias hangs back, sits down.

Catherine: “How often are these tours given?”

Arwyn smiles. “This one is nearly to a close. I believe you’re part of my next group. We’ll commence at the Weston Gallery, Roman Britain. in twenty minutes.”

Catherine gathers the others and they head to the gallery. Matthias shifts his Share the Senses to a guard in the room with the cap.

Gwenllian approaches calmly, confidently. “I believe you’re my next tour group.” She then looks to Tony, clasps him by his hands. “It’s been so long. It is good to see you.” Tony is a little taken aback; he wasn’t expecting recognition, or warmth. Arwyn pivots to Kim Sun. “We can catch up after the tour.” She then strides forward, walking through the galleries and the group follows. She’s passionate and knowledgeable about the exhibits, and the group starts to realize that Arwyn is a contemporary of some of these millenia-old artifacts.

sections.title: Roman Britain Exhibit
sections.text:
Ferhat, Matthias, Oliver, Kim, Catherine, Tony, Alice, Gwenllian

Arwyn seems unflappable, except to Matthias who thinks something is irritating her. Nevertheless, she seems to be at ease, despite all the mortals surrounding them.

They move into the Roman exhibit, and the detailed stories of her stories settle into a more typical tour guide spiel. Matthias is scoping the place out, figuring out how to pull off a heist.

As they get close to the cap, about 40 feet away, they see an elderly couple reading the placard near the cap, and Catherine turns to Gwenllian.

Catherine: “Would you help us retrieve that cap? It’s herald business.”

Gwenllian stops abruptly and turns rigidly towards Catherine. “I have served my god lng and faithfully. I’ve seen him lift his servants into the light and I’ve seen him reduce his enemies to ash. It is the sun’s prerogative todo as he sees fit — as he did with you. Do you know? What was done to you?”

Catherine: “No.”

Gwenllian: “You bear my blood, and the blood of all those who most closely served. I do not know if you have retained a soul; that was the price of the level of duty he demanded of you.”

Alice speaks up. “I will fulfill my duty to bring him back; we need the cap to do so. He is amongst us.”

Gwenllian stands tall and snarls, and speaks loudly. “Excuse me! This area of the museum needs to be cleared.” She directs people to the exits, amid their mutterings and grumblings, and then directs the security guard out as well.

Alice has an epiphany; she remembers the failed prior attempts of the Blooding, and how her receiving this ritual was meant to obliterate her individuality and make her the perfect herald, the perfect obedient servant.

She’s somehow been able to claw back parts of herself, but also realizes that these flashbacks are memories, memories from the blood of those who contributed.

With the room empty, Gwenllian walks up to the case, scans her retina, unlocks the case and retrieves the cap. She hands it gently to Alice.

Matthias is dumbfounded that they just asked for it and got it.

Alice: “I think we’re done here.”

Catherine, to Arwyn: “Come with us? You could witness his return.”

Gwenllian: “I’ve stayed here as long as I have, honestly, to protect the artifact; the artifact you now hold. So yes.” She looks to Kim, and nods. “I’ll come with you. Has the Prince made a ruling yet?” Kim shakes her head.

Catherine: “We have not been able to reach Queen Anne since Elysium.”

Alice: “Why did you do what you did?”

Gwenllian looks a little bewildered. “I think the accusation is correct. I think I did kill him. I don’t remember doing it. I remember going to Bath to meet him, and I remember having returned and hearing about his death.”

Arwyn leads them down into the lower levels and service corridors. They emerge a few blocks from the museum. They debate where to go, and eventually Arwyn is convinced to stay with Catherine and the others. She sends Kim back to Chun Hei.

They tell Gwenllian about Richard de Worde. Alice shows the necklaces she’s made. Matthias mentions his mapping efforts and rat army. Tony talks about the dossiers. Gwenllian agrees to join them in the underground.

Alice found a book with a ritual for restoring memory. It seems doable.

Matthias wants to use Spirits Touch on Gwenllian’s tooth. Lady Catherine tries to sweet talk Arwyn, and she is *not* having it, and when Catherine leans into her domination, Arwyn’s eyes flash and she commands Catherine to step away, who does so immediately.

Alice steps in and tries to explain Matthias’ intent. Gwenllian responds: “Of all people, I would have expected a Tremere to understand how giving something of oneself to another irreparably exposes you. I will not give something of myself to anyone but my Lord.”

Matthias clarifies that all he needs to do is touch it. Eventually, after a lot of arguing, Gwenllian accepts and pulls the tooth. She holds it out to Matthias, and turns to Alice. “I had been a kindred for a millenia before Tremere killed Saulah.”

Matthias touches the tooth and gets a fast-forward. Gwenllian kills but does not diablerize Jackdaw. She disposes of the body, and then reports to Queen Anne, who wipes her memory.”

Matthias shares this. Alice: “The bitch!”

Gwenllian has a sober look. “That will have been the last time.”

The five of them put on the necklaces, Matthias’ rats and dog follow, and they head into the underground to confront Richard de Worde.

rules.title: Boon levels
rules.text: Below are examples of a boon’s worth. However, boons are always on a case-by-case basis in value. A boon that is a minor boon from a neonate may be a major boon from a fledgling. The classification of boons depends on fulfillment ability, which can hinge on the power, the circumstance, or the difficulty for the granter. It can also be classified based on desperation as well, upping the ante for something they need immediately, also known as sweetening the deal. If an example is needed, a major boon for a neonate could be a trivial boon for a Prince.[[1]](https://vtm.paradoxwikis.com/Boons#cite_note-:0-1)

sections.title: Trivial boon
sections.text:
There is no risk or cost to the granter, these might nor even by tracked within a coterie.

- Helping to find blood for the night.
- Getting an invitation to an exclusive or popular nightclub.
- Making space in a haven.

sections.title: Minor boon
sections.text:
There is an effort to this boon, going out of one’s way. They have some risks to them.

- Vote in favor of another but only if there is minimal social harm.
- Kill an unimportant human in the way.
- Providing refuge to someone in dire need such as sanctuary or sustenance.
- Providing access to ancient tomes.

sections.title: Major boon
sections.text:
Not given lightly as the risk and expense can be so great.

- Granting rich hunting grounds to another.
- Revealing a major secret.
- Leveraging their own resources towards someone else's agenda.
- Changing one's expected vote in the council.

sections.title: Life boon
sections.text:
Very rare and usually only given when [Final Death](https://vtm.paradoxwikis.com/Final_Death) or the death of a [Touchstone](https://vtm.paradoxwikis.com/Touchstone) is on the horizon.

- The desperate attempt to save own unlife
- The desperate attempt to save touchstone’s life
- Keeping a deadly secret

Ghouls

[Image: Untitled.png](campaign/assets/gm/rules-quickreference-untitled.webp)

Feeding a mortal vitae one time will make them a ghoul. They will also be one step closer to a full Blood Bond and be more inclined towards a positive reaction to you. It takes three drinks over 3 separate occasions to produce a full Blood Bond and can be raised to a “total” of 6, meaning it becomes nearly impossible for the ghoul to disobey or act against their regnant in any way. Additionally, a ghoul must be fed vitae at least once a month to retain their condition but it does not have to be the vitae of their original Regnant.

Ghoul
Ghouls form the stock of retainers, servants, and slaves of many
Kindred. Addicted to the vitae
in their masters’ and mistresses’
dead veins, ghouls will obey their
creators in any way they can,
even to the point of injury, and
in some cases, death. Ghouls may
be stoic butlers, steady bodyguards, or blood-crazed savages,
depending on their regnant.
Standard Dice Pools: Physical 4,
Social 4, Mental 4
Secondary Attributes: Health 6,
Willpower 5
Exceptional Dice Pools: Awareness 6, Intimidation 5, Occult 6,
Stealth 5
Disciplines: One Discipline at 1
See p. 234 for more on Ghouls.
